# Page: Data Processing Pipeline

# Data Processing Pipeline

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py](deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page provides an overview of the end-to-end data processing workflow in DeepSpot2Cell, from raw HEST-1k data to training-ready datasets. The pipeline transforms whole slide images (WSI) and spatial transcriptomics data into pre-computed embeddings and expression matrices that can be efficiently loaded during model training and inference.

For detailed implementation of dataset creation, see [Dataset Creation](#5.1). For information about data preprocessing and normalization strategies, see [Data Preprocessing and Normalization](#5.2). For information about how the processed data is loaded during training, see [DS2CDataset and Data Loading](#4.2).

**Sources**: [README.md:1-70](), [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:1-536]()

---

## Overview

The data processing pipeline consists of four main stages that separate computationally expensive preprocessing from model training:

1. **Data Acquisition**: Access raw data from HEST-1k dataset including H&E whole slide images, spatial transcriptomics measurements, and cell segmentation masks
2. **Tile Generation and Feature Extraction**: Extract cell and spot tiles from WSI, compute morphological embeddings using Pathology Foundation Models (PFMs)
3. **Dataset Persistence**: Save pre-computed embeddings and expression data in efficient formats (.npy and .h5 files)
4. **Data Loading for Training**: Load and batch the processed data during model training with optional augmentation

This modular design allows the expensive PFM feature extraction (Stage 2) to be performed once, with the pre-computed embeddings reused across multiple training experiments.

**Sources**: [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:165-492]()

---

## End-to-End Pipeline Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Stage1["Stage 1: Data Acquisition"]
        HEST["HEST-1k Dataset<br/>iter_hest()"]
        WSI["H&E Whole Slide Images<br/>.tif files"]
        TRANS["Spatial Transcriptomics<br/>transcript_df"]
        SEG["Cell Segmentation<br/>get_shapes('xenium_cell')"]
        TISSUE["Tissue Masks<br/>*_contours.geojson"]
    end
    
    subgraph Stage2["Stage 2: Tile Generation & Feature Extraction"]
        CELL_PROC["Cell Processing<br/>filtered_df.groupby('cell_id')"]
        CROP_CELL["Crop Cell Tiles<br/>crop_tile()"]
        PATCH_PROC["Patch Processing<br/>num_patches_h x num_patches_w"]
        CROP_SPOT["Crop Spot Tiles<br/>crop_tile()"]
        PFM["PFM Feature Extraction<br/>process_batch()<br/>get_spot_embs()"]
    end
    
    subgraph Stage3["Stage 3: Dataset Persistence"]
        NPY["Embeddings Storage<br/>{patch_barcode}.npy<br/>embeddings{variant}/{model}/"]
        H5["Expression Storage<br/>{sample_id}_expressions.h5<br/>expressions{variant}/"]
        META["Metadata<br/>cell_ids, centroids, bboxes"]
    end
    
    subgraph Stage4["Stage 4: Data Loading"]
        DATASET["DS2CDataset<br/>deepspot2cell/dataloader.py"]
        LOADER["DataLoader<br/>batching + masking"]
    end
    
    HEST --> WSI
    HEST --> TRANS
    HEST --> SEG
    HEST --> TISSUE
    
    TRANS --> CELL_PROC
    SEG --> CELL_PROC
    WSI --> CROP_CELL
    CELL_PROC --> CROP_CELL
    
    WSI --> CROP_SPOT
    TISSUE --> PATCH_PROC
    PATCH_PROC --> CROP_SPOT
    
    CROP_CELL --> PFM
    CROP_SPOT --> PFM
    
    PFM --> NPY
    CELL_PROC --> H5
    PATCH_PROC --> H5
    CELL_PROC --> META
    
    NPY --> DATASET
    H5 --> DATASET
    META --> DATASET
    DATASET --> LOADER
    
    LOADER --> TRAIN["Model Training<br/>scripts/train.py"]
```

**Diagram 1: End-to-End Data Processing Pipeline** - This diagram shows the complete data flow from HEST-1k acquisition through to model training, highlighting the key processing functions and file formats at each stage.

**Sources**: [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:165-536](), [README.md:24-33]()

---

## Pipeline Stages

### Stage 1: Data Acquisition

The pipeline begins by accessing data from the HEST-1k dataset using the HEST library's iterator:

```mermaid
graph LR
    ITER["iter_hest()<br/>data_folder, id_list"]
    ST["STObject"]
    
    subgraph Data["STObject Contents"]
        WSI_F["WSI File<br/>{sample_id}.tif"]
        ADATA["adata<br/>gene expression"]
        TRANS_DF["transcript_df<br/>cell-level transcripts"]
        SHAPES["Cell Shapes<br/>get_shapes('xenium_cell', 'he')"]
    end
    
    META_F["Metadata<br/>{sample_id}.json"]
    TISSUE_F["Tissue Segmentation<br/>{sample_id}_contours.geojson"]
    
    ITER --> ST
    ST --> WSI_F
    ST --> ADATA
    ST --> TRANS_DF
    ST --> SHAPES
    
    META_F --> PIXEL_SIZE["pixel_size_um_estimated"]
    TISSUE_F --> MASK["create_tissue_mask()"]
```

**Diagram 2: Data Acquisition Components** - Shows how raw data is accessed from HEST-1k and auxiliary metadata files.

| Data Component | Source | Purpose |
|---------------|--------|---------|
| WSI Image | `{data_folder}/wsis/{sample_id}.tif` | Source for tile extraction |
| Transcript Data | `st.transcript_df` | Cell-level gene expression counts |
| Cell Shapes | `st.get_shapes('xenium_cell', 'he')` | Cell boundaries for cropping |
| Metadata | `{data_folder}/metadata/{sample_id}.json` | Pixel size calibration |
| Tissue Mask | `{data_folder}/tissue_seg/{sample_id}_contours.geojson` | Spatial filtering |

**Sources**: [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:165-203](), [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:188-190]()

---

### Stage 2: Tile Generation and Feature Extraction

This stage performs the computationally intensive operations: extracting image tiles and computing PFM embeddings.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph CellProcessing["Cell-Level Processing"]
        FILTER["Transcript Filtering<br/>qv > threshold<br/>cell_id != UNASSIGNED"]
        GROUP["Group by Cell<br/>filtered_df.groupby('cell_id')"]
        EXPR["Compute Expression<br/>gene_counts per cell"]
        GEOM["Get Cell Geometry<br/>cell_shapes[cell_id]"]
        CROP_C["Crop Cell Tile<br/>crop_tile(wsi, square_bbox)"]
        BATCH_C["Batch Cells<br/>process_batch()"]
    end
    
    subgraph PatchProcessing["Patch-Level Processing"]
        GRID["Grid WSI<br/>num_patches_h x num_patches_w"]
        CENTER["Compute Patch Center<br/>patch_x + patch_size // 2"]
        TISSUE_CHK["Check Tissue Mask<br/>tissue_mask.contains(center)"]
        CROP_P["Crop Patch Tile<br/>crop_tile(wsi, patch_x, patch_y)"]
        SPOT_DEF["Define Spot Region<br/>Point(center).buffer(radius)"]
        ASSIGN["Assign Cells to Spot<br/>intersection >= 0.6"]
        AGG["Aggregate Expression<br/>sum cells '_in' spot"]
        BATCH_P["Get Spot Embedding<br/>get_spot_embs()"]
    end
    
    FILTER --> GROUP
    GROUP --> EXPR
    GROUP --> GEOM
    GEOM --> CROP_C
    CROP_C --> BATCH_C
    
    GRID --> CENTER
    CENTER --> TISSUE_CHK
    TISSUE_CHK -->|"inside tissue"| CROP_P
    CROP_P --> SPOT_DEF
    SPOT_DEF --> ASSIGN
    ASSIGN --> AGG
    CROP_P --> BATCH_P
    
    BATCH_C --> EMB_C["Cell Embeddings"]
    BATCH_P --> EMB_P["Spot Embeddings"]
```

**Diagram 3: Tile Generation and Feature Extraction** - Details the parallel processing of cells and patches, including geometric operations and PFM embedding computation.

#### Cell Processing

The cell processing loop [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:238-327]() performs the following operations for each cell:

1. **Filter transcripts** by quality value (`qv > qv_thr`) and valid cell assignment
2. **Compute gene expression vector** by counting transcripts per gene for each cell
3. **Extract cell geometry** from segmentation masks and validate
4. **Compute square bounding box** centered on cell centroid to contain entire cell
5. **Crop cell tile** from WSI using `crop_tile()`
6. **Batch process** cells through PFM using `process_batch()` for efficiency

#### Patch Processing

The patch processing loop [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:340-469]() divides the WSI into a regular grid:

1. **Grid generation**: WSI divided into patches of size `patch_size` (typically 55μm)
2. **Tissue filtering**: Skip patches whose center falls outside tissue mask
3. **Cell assignment**: Find cells within patch using spatial bounding box queries
4. **Spot definition**: Create circular spot region (radius = `spot_diameter/2`) centered on patch
5. **Cell tagging**: Tag cells as "in" spot if >60% overlap, "out" otherwise
6. **Expression aggregation**: Sum expression of all cells tagged "in" to get spot expression
7. **Spot embedding**: Compute embedding of full patch tile using `get_spot_embs()`

**Sources**: [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:23-59](), [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:208-327](), [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:340-469]()

---

### Stage 3: Dataset Persistence

Processed data is saved in two file formats optimized for different access patterns:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph EmbeddingFiles["Embedding Files (.npy)"]
        NPY_PATH["embeddings{variant}/{model_name}/{patch_barcode}.npy"]
        NPY_STRUCT["Array Structure:<br/>[0] = spot_embedding<br/>[1:N] = cell_embeddings"]
        NPY_DTYPE["dtype: float16<br/>shape: (N_cells+1, feature_dim)"]
    end
    
    subgraph ExpressionFiles["Expression Files (.h5)"]
        H5_PATH["expressions{variant}/{sample_id}_expressions.h5"]
        
        subgraph H5_GROUP["HDF5 Group: {patch_barcode}"]
            H5_SPOT["spot_expression<br/>aggregated counts"]
            H5_CELLS["cell_expressions<br/>individual cell counts"]
            H5_IDS["cell_ids<br/>tagged '_in' or '_out'"]
            H5_CENT["cell_centroids<br/>normalized coordinates"]
            H5_BBOX["cell_bbxs<br/>normalized bounding boxes"]
        end
        
        H5_ATTRS["Attributes:<br/>spot_diameter, patch_size<br/>um_per_px"]
    end
    
    PROC["process_sample()"]
    
    PROC --> NPY_PATH
    NPY_PATH --> NPY_STRUCT
    NPY_STRUCT --> NPY_DTYPE
    
    PROC --> H5_PATH
    H5_PATH --> H5_GROUP
    H5_GROUP --> H5_SPOT
    H5_GROUP --> H5_CELLS
    H5_GROUP --> H5_IDS
    H5_GROUP --> H5_CENT
    H5_GROUP --> H5_BBOX
    H5_PATH --> H5_ATTRS
```

**Diagram 4: Data Persistence Structure** - Shows the file organization and data structures used for storing processed datasets.

#### Embedding Files (.npy)

One `.npy` file is created per patch, containing embeddings for the spot and all associated cells [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:458-468]():

- **Location**: `{data_folder}/embeddings{dataset_variant}/{model_name}/{patch_barcode}.npy`
- **Format**: NumPy array with shape `(N_cells + 1, feature_dim)`
- **Content**: 
  - Index 0: Spot (patch) embedding from PFM
  - Indices 1 to N: Cell embeddings from PFM, one per cell in patch
- **Data type**: `float16` for space efficiency

#### Expression Files (.h5)

One `.h5` file is created per sample, containing all patches for that sample [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:474-487]():

- **Location**: `{data_folder}/expressions{dataset_variant}/{sample_id}_expressions.h5`
- **Format**: HDF5 with hierarchical group structure
- **Groups**: One group per patch, named by `patch_barcode`
- **Datasets per group**:
  - `spot_expression`: Aggregated gene expression for the spot
  - `cell_expressions`: Individual gene expression vectors for each cell
  - `cell_ids`: Cell identifiers with `_in`/`_out` tags indicating spot membership
  - `cell_centroids`: Normalized (x, y) coordinates relative to patch
  - `cell_bbxs`: Normalized bounding boxes (minx, miny, maxx, maxy)
- **Attributes**: `spot_diameter`, `patch_size`, `um_per_px` for spatial calibration

**Sources**: [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:458-487]()

---

### Stage 4: Data Loading for Training

The `DS2CDataset` class loads the pre-computed data during training:

```mermaid
graph LR
    CONFIG["Training Config<br/>configs/*.yaml"]
    
    subgraph DATASET["DS2CDataset.__init__()"]
        LOAD_H5["Load Expression HDF5<br/>h5py.File()"]
        LIST_NPY["List Embedding Files<br/>glob embeddings/*.npy"]
        FILTER["Filter by Split<br/>train/val/test"]
        INDEX["Build Index<br/>patch_barcode -> files"]
    end
    
    subgraph GETITEM["DS2CDataset.__getitem__()"]
        READ_H5["Read from HDF5<br/>spot_group[key]"]
        READ_NPY["Read from NPY<br/>np.load()"]
        PARSE["Parse Embeddings<br/>spot_emb, cell_embs"]
        MASK["Create Mask<br/>valid cells"]
        NORM["Normalize Expression<br/>standard_scale()"]
    end
    
    CONFIG --> DATASET
    DATASET --> LOAD_H5
    DATASET --> LIST_NPY
    DATASET --> FILTER
    FILTER --> INDEX
    
    INDEX --> GETITEM
    GETITEM --> READ_H5
    GETITEM --> READ_NPY
    READ_NPY --> PARSE
    READ_H5 --> NORM
    PARSE --> MASK
    
    MASK --> BATCH["DataLoader Batching"]
    NORM --> BATCH
```

**Diagram 5: Data Loading Pipeline** - Shows how `DS2CDataset` loads and preprocesses the persistent data during training.

The dataset class handles:
- **Lazy loading**: Files are opened but data read only when requested via `__getitem__()`
- **Indexing**: Maps patch barcodes to file locations for efficient lookup
- **Filtering**: Applies dataset splits (train/val/test) based on configuration
- **Preprocessing**: Normalizes expression data and creates attention masks
- **Batching**: Integrates with PyTorch `DataLoader` for mini-batch training

For detailed implementation, see [DS2CDataset and Data Loading](#4.2).

**Sources**: [deepspot2cell/dataloader.py]() (referenced but not provided in full)

---

## File Organization

The data processing pipeline creates the following directory structure:

```
{data_folder}/
├── wsis/
│   └── {sample_id}.tif                    # H&E whole slide images
├── metadata/
│   └── {sample_id}.json                   # Pixel size and other metadata
├── tissue_seg/
│   └── {sample_id}_contours.geojson       # Tissue segmentation masks
├── embeddings{dataset_variant}/
│   └── {model_name}/
│       └── patch_{h}_{w}_{sample_id}.npy  # Pre-computed embeddings
└── expressions{dataset_variant}/
    └── {sample_id}_expressions.h5         # Gene expression data
```

The `{dataset_variant}` suffix (e.g., `_v1`, `_test`) allows multiple processed versions of the same raw data to coexist.

**Sources**: [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:529-531]()

---

## Processing Configuration

The data processing pipeline is controlled via YAML configuration files (typically `configs/dataset.*.yaml`):

| Configuration Parameter | Location | Purpose |
|------------------------|----------|---------|
| `data_folder` | `data.data_folder` | Root directory for all data |
| `model_name` | `data.model_name` | PFM identifier (e.g., "UNI", "hoptimus0") |
| `model_path` | `data.model_path` | Path to PFM checkpoint |
| `dataset_variant` | `data.dataset_variant` | Suffix for output directories |
| `spot_diameter` | `data.spot_diameter` | Spot diameter in micrometers (default: 55) |
| `patch_size` | `data.patch_size` | Patch size in micrometers |
| `qv_thr` | `data.qv_thr` | Quality value threshold for transcript filtering |
| `dataset_ids` | `data.{dataset}.train.dataset_ids` | List of sample IDs to process |
| `ordered_genes_file` | `data.{dataset}.ordered_genes_file` | Gene ordering specification |
| `gpu_batch_size` | `processing.gpu_batch_size` | Batch size for GPU processing |
| `cpu_batch_size` | `processing.cpu_batch_size` | Batch size for CPU processing |

For complete configuration details, see [Dataset Configuration](#6.1).

**Sources**: [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:495-536](), [deepspot2cell/utils/utils.py]() (referenced)

---

## Key Processing Functions

### `process_sample()`

The main processing function that orchestrates the entire pipeline for a single sample.

**Signature**: `process_sample(sample_id, st, model, preprocess, device, batch_size, config)`

**Location**: [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:165-492]()

**Workflow**:
1. Load metadata and compute spatial parameters
2. Sort genes by variability
3. Create tissue mask from GeoJSON
4. Process all cells: extract tiles, compute embeddings
5. Process all patches: assign cells, aggregate expression, compute embeddings
6. Save embeddings as `.npy` files
7. Save expression data as `.h5` file

### `process_batch()`

Batch processes image tiles through the PFM for efficient GPU utilization.

**Signature**: `process_batch(batch_patches, model, preprocess, device)`

**Location**: [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:23-40]()

**Details**:
- Handles image preprocessing and tensor conversion
- Uses automatic mixed precision (AMP) on CUDA devices
- Processes in batches to maximize GPU throughput
- Returns embeddings on CPU for memory efficiency

### `get_spot_embs()`

Computes embedding for a single spot tile.

**Signature**: `get_spot_embs(X_spot, morphology_model, preprocess, device, dtype_to_use=torch.float16)`

**Location**: [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:43-58]()

### `crop_tile()`

Extracts a rectangular tile from the whole slide image using PyVips.

**Signature**: `crop_tile(image, x_pixel, y_pixel, spot_diameter)`

**Location**: [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:87-93]()

**Note**: Returns tiles as NumPy arrays with shape `(height, width, 3)` for RGB channels.

### `create_tissue_mask()`

Creates a unified tissue mask from GeoJSON polygons with robust error handling.

**Signature**: `create_tissue_mask(tissue_mask_json, sample_id)`

**Location**: [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:113-162]()

**Features**:
- Validates and fixes invalid polygon geometries
- Merges multiple tissue polygons using `unary_union`
- Provides fallback strategies if union fails
- Reports statistics on valid/invalid polygons

**Sources**: [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:23-162]()

---

## Performance Considerations

The data processing pipeline is designed for efficiency:

1. **One-time computation**: PFM embeddings are computed once and reused across training runs
2. **Batch processing**: Cells and spots are processed in batches to maximize GPU utilization
3. **Memory management**: Embeddings stored as `float16` to reduce disk space
4. **Compression**: Expression data in HDF5 uses gzip compression (level 4)
5. **Lazy loading**: Training dataset loads data on-demand rather than all at once
6. **Progress tracking**: Processing functions report progress with ETA estimates

Typical processing times on GPU (example from code output):
- **Cell processing**: ~10-30 seconds per 10,000 cells
- **Patch processing**: ~1-5 seconds per 1,000 patches
- **Complete sample**: 5-20 minutes depending on tissue size

**Sources**: [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:234-246](), [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:344-349]()

---

## Command Line Usage

The dataset creation script can be invoked from the command line:

```bash
python -m deepspot2cell.dataset_creation \
    --config configs/dataset.example.yaml \
    --dataset lung \
    --indices 0 1 2
```

**Arguments**:
- `--config`: Path to configuration file (default: `configs/dataset.example.yaml`)
- `--dataset`: Dataset identifier matching config file keys (default: `lung`)
- `--indices`: Optional list of specific sample indices to process (processes all if omitted)

The script automatically detects available hardware and sets batch sizes accordingly [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:514-524]().

**Sources**: [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:495-536]()

# Page: Dataset Creation

# Dataset Creation

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [configs/dataset.example.yaml](configs/dataset.example.yaml)
- [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py](deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This document describes the dataset creation pipeline that transforms raw HEST-1k spatial transcriptomics data into training-ready embeddings and expression files. The pipeline processes whole-slide H&E images and cell-level transcript data to generate morphological embeddings using Pathology Foundation Models (PFMs) and organize gene expression data at both cell and spot levels.

For information about using these preprocessed datasets during training, see [DS2CDataset and Data Loading](#4.2). For details on the HEST-1k dataset structure and access, see [HEST-1k Dataset](#10.1). For configuration options, see [Dataset Configuration](#6.1).

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:1-536](), [configs/dataset.example.yaml:1-27]()

## Overview

The dataset creation process is implemented in [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py]() and is typically run once per dataset as a preprocessing step before training. It performs computationally intensive operations—PFM feature extraction, spatial filtering, and data organization—that would be inefficient to repeat during each training run.

```mermaid
graph TB
    CONFIG["dataset.example.yaml<br/>Configuration File"]
    HEST_DATA["HEST Data Directory"]
    
    subgraph "Input Data"
        WSI["WSI Images<br/>wsis/{sample_id}.tif"]
        TRANSCRIPTS["Transcript Data<br/>ST object transcripts"]
        CELL_SEG["Cell Segmentation<br/>xenium_cell shapes"]
        TISSUE_MASK["Tissue Masks<br/>tissue_seg/{sample_id}_contours.geojson"]
        METADATA["Sample Metadata<br/>metadata/{sample_id}.json"]
    end
    
    subgraph "process_sample()"
        LOAD["Load Sample Data<br/>via iter_hest()"]
        FILTER["Filter Transcripts<br/>by qv_thr quality"]
        CELL_PROC["Cell Processing Loop<br/>extract + embed cells"]
        PATCH_PROC["Patch Processing Loop<br/>extract + embed patches"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Helper Functions"
        CROP["crop_tile()<br/>Extract image regions"]
        BATCH["process_batch()<br/>Batch PFM inference"]
        SPOT_EMB["get_spot_embs()<br/>Spot embedding"]
        TISSUE["create_tissue_mask()<br/>Polygon union"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Files"
        NPY["Embeddings<br/>embeddings/{model}/{patch_barcode}.npy"]
        H5["Expressions<br/>expressions/{sample_id}_expressions.h5"]
    end
    
    CONFIG --> LOAD
    HEST_DATA --> WSI
    HEST_DATA --> TRANSCRIPTS
    HEST_DATA --> CELL_SEG
    HEST_DATA --> TISSUE_MASK
    HEST_DATA --> METADATA
    
    WSI --> LOAD
    TRANSCRIPTS --> LOAD
    CELL_SEG --> LOAD
    TISSUE_MASK --> TISSUE
    METADATA --> LOAD
    
    LOAD --> FILTER
    FILTER --> CELL_PROC
    CELL_PROC --> PATCH_PROC
    
    CELL_PROC --> CROP
    CELL_PROC --> BATCH
    PATCH_PROC --> CROP
    PATCH_PROC --> BATCH
    PATCH_PROC --> SPOT_EMB
    
    TISSUE --> CELL_PROC
    TISSUE --> PATCH_PROC
    
    PATCH_PROC --> NPY
    PATCH_PROC --> H5
```

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:165-536](), [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:495-536]()

## Input Requirements

The dataset creation pipeline expects a HEST-formatted data directory with the following structure:

| Directory/File | Description | Used By |
|----------------|-------------|---------|
| `wsis/{sample_id}.tif` | Whole-slide H&E image (PyVips format) | [crop_tile():87-93]() |
| `metadata/{sample_id}.json` | Sample metadata (pixel size, cell counts) | [process_sample():173-183]() |
| `tissue_seg/{sample_id}_contours.geojson` | Tissue segmentation polygons | [create_tissue_mask():113-162]() |
| HEST ST object | Spatial transcriptomics data (transcripts, cell shapes) | [process_sample():193-208]() |

The configuration file (`configs/dataset.example.yaml`) specifies:

```yaml
data:
  data_folder: /path/to/hest_data
  dataset_variant: _v1                    # Output directory suffix
  model_name: phikonv2                    # PFM to use
  model_path: /path/to/phikonv2
  
  spot_diameter_px: 160                   # Spot diameter (pixels)
  patch_size_px: 224                      # Patch size (pixels)
  qv_thr: 20                              # Transcript quality threshold
  
  lung:
    ordered_genes_file: lung_ordered_genes.json
    train:
      dataset_ids: [SAMPLE_ID_1, ...]    # Samples to process
```

**Sources:** [configs/dataset.example.yaml:1-27](), [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:166-183]()

## Processing Pipeline

### Configuration and Initialization

The main script parses command-line arguments and loads the configuration:

```bash
python deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py \
    --config configs/dataset.example.yaml \
    --dataset lung \
    --indices 0 1 2
```

The script automatically selects the device and batch size based on available hardware:

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:495-527]()

### Sample Processing Workflow

The `process_sample()` function [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:165-492]() implements the core processing logic for each sample:

```mermaid
graph TB
    START["process_sample(sample_id, st, model, ...)"]
    
    CHECK["Check if already processed<br/>{sample_id}_expressions.h5 exists"]
    SKIP["Skip sample"]
    
    META["Load metadata<br/>pixel_size_um, spot_diameter, patch_size"]
    GENES["Order genes<br/>sort_genes_by_variability()"]
    MASK["Create tissue mask<br/>create_tissue_mask()"]
    
    CELL_INIT["Initialize cell_dict = {}"]
    CELL_LOOP["For each cell in filtered_df.groupby('cell_id')"]
    CELL_CHECK["Check: zero expression?<br/>invalid geometry?<br/>outside tissue?"]
    CELL_SKIP["Skip cell"]
    CELL_CROP["Crop cell image<br/>crop_tile()"]
    CELL_BATCH["Add to batch"]
    CELL_EMBED["process_batch()<br/>when batch full"]
    CELL_STORE["Store in cell_dict"]
    
    PATCH_INIT["Initialize spot_dict = {}"]
    PATCH_LOOP["For each patch (h_idx, w_idx)"]
    PATCH_CHECK["Check: outside tissue?<br/>no nearby cells?"]
    PATCH_SKIP["Skip patch"]
    PATCH_CROP["Crop patch image<br/>crop_tile()"]
    PATCH_CELLS["Assign cells to patch<br/>spatial intersection"]
    PATCH_SPOT["Compute spot expression<br/>aggregate '_in' cells"]
    PATCH_EMB_SPOT["get_spot_embs()<br/>spot embedding"]
    PATCH_EMB_CELLS["Load cell embeddings<br/>from cell_dict"]
    PATCH_SAVE_NPY["Save .npy<br/>embeddings/{model}/{patch_barcode}.npy"]
    PATCH_STORE["Store in spot_dict"]
    
    SAVE_H5["Save HDF5<br/>expressions/{sample_id}_expressions.h5"]
    END["Cleanup: del spot_dict, cell_dict, gc.collect()"]
    
    START --> CHECK
    CHECK -->|exists| SKIP
    CHECK -->|not exists| META
    META --> GENES
    GENES --> MASK
    
    MASK --> CELL_INIT
    CELL_INIT --> CELL_LOOP
    CELL_LOOP --> CELL_CHECK
    CELL_CHECK -->|skip| CELL_SKIP
    CELL_CHECK -->|valid| CELL_CROP
    CELL_CROP --> CELL_BATCH
    CELL_BATCH --> CELL_EMBED
    CELL_EMBED --> CELL_STORE
    CELL_STORE --> CELL_LOOP
    CELL_SKIP --> CELL_LOOP
    
    CELL_LOOP -->|done| PATCH_INIT
    PATCH_INIT --> PATCH_LOOP
    PATCH_LOOP --> PATCH_CHECK
    PATCH_CHECK -->|skip| PATCH_SKIP
    PATCH_CHECK -->|valid| PATCH_CROP
    PATCH_CROP --> PATCH_CELLS
    PATCH_CELLS --> PATCH_SPOT
    PATCH_SPOT --> PATCH_EMB_SPOT
    PATCH_EMB_SPOT --> PATCH_EMB_CELLS
    PATCH_EMB_CELLS --> PATCH_SAVE_NPY
    PATCH_SAVE_NPY --> PATCH_STORE
    PATCH_STORE --> PATCH_LOOP
    PATCH_SKIP --> PATCH_LOOP
    
    PATCH_LOOP -->|done| SAVE_H5
    SAVE_H5 --> END
```

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:165-492]()

### Cell Processing

The cell processing loop [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:238-327]() extracts individual cell data and morphological embeddings:

#### Transcript Filtering

Before processing cells, transcripts are filtered by quality:

```python
filtered_df = st.transcript_df[~st.transcript_df.cell_id.isin(['UNASSIGNED', -1])]
filtered_df = filtered_df[filtered_df['qv'] > qv_thr]  # Quality value threshold
```

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:207-225]()

#### Cell Data Extraction

For each cell identified by `cell_id`:

1. **Gene Expression Aggregation**: Count transcripts per gene [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:248-255]()
2. **Cell Shape**: Extract polygon from `cell_shapes` [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:257-267]()
3. **Spatial Filtering**: Check if cell centroid is inside tissue mask [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:272-275]()
4. **Bounding Box**: Compute smallest square containing the cell [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:278-288]()
5. **Image Cropping**: Extract cell image region using `crop_tile()` [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:290-294]()

#### Batch Embedding

Cells are processed in batches through the PFM:

```mermaid
graph LR
    CELLS["Cell Images<br/>accumulated in batch"]
    PROC["process_batch()<br/>preprocess + resize"]
    TENSOR["torch.stack()<br/>batch tensor"]
    PFM["PFM Model<br/>model(batch_tensor)"]
    EMB["Embeddings<br/>detach().cpu()"]
    STORE["Store in cell_dict"]
    
    CELLS --> PROC
    PROC --> TENSOR
    TENSOR --> PFM
    PFM --> EMB
    EMB --> STORE
```

The `process_batch()` function [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:23-40]() handles:
- Image preprocessing (resize to square if needed)
- Conversion to tensors with appropriate dtype (float16 for GPU, float32 for CPU)
- Automatic mixed precision (AMP) when using CUDA
- Batch inference with gradient disabled

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:23-40](), [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:306-316]()

### Patch/Spot Processing

The patch processing loop [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:340-488]() divides the WSI into a grid and processes each patch as a spot:

#### Spatial Grid

The WSI is divided into non-overlapping patches:

```python
num_patches_h = wsi_height // patch_size
num_patches_w = wsi_width // patch_size
```

Each patch is identified by `patch_barcode = f"patch_{h_idx}_{w_idx}_{sample_id}"`

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:200-205](), [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:351]()

#### Cell-to-Patch Assignment

For each patch, nearby cells are identified and assigned based on spatial relationships:

```mermaid
graph TB
    PATCH["Patch (224×224 px)<br/>patch_box"]
    SPOT["Spot Circle<br/>55μm diameter<br/>centered on patch"]
    
    subgraph "Cell Assignment Logic"
        SEARCH["Find nearby cells<br/>within search_radius"]
        INTERSECT["Check cell.intersects(patch_box)"]
        OVERLAP["Calculate intersection.area / cell.area"]
        THRESHOLD["threshold >= 0.6?"]
        SPOT_CHECK["Check cell.intersection(spot).area / cell.area"]
        TAG["Tag: '_in' if >= 0.6<br/>else '_out'"]
    end
    
    OUTPUT["Cell assigned to patch<br/>with tag '_in' or '_out'"]
    
    PATCH --> SEARCH
    SEARCH --> INTERSECT
    INTERSECT -->|no| SKIP["Skip cell"]
    INTERSECT -->|yes| OVERLAP
    OVERLAP --> THRESHOLD
    THRESHOLD -->|no| SKIP
    THRESHOLD -->|yes| SPOT_CHECK
    SPOT_CHECK --> TAG
    TAG --> OUTPUT
```

Key criteria [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:390-434]():
- Cell must have at least 60% of its area within the patch bounds
- Cells are tagged `_in` if ≥60% overlaps with the spot circle (55μm diameter)
- Cells are tagged `_out` if <60% overlaps with the spot circle
- Only `_in` cells contribute to spot-level gene expression

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:362-454]()

#### Spot Expression Aggregation

The spot-level gene expression is computed by summing expression from all `_in` cells:

```python
spot_expression = np.zeros(len(ordered_gene_names))
for i, cell_id in enumerate(cell_ids_tagged):
    if '_in' in cell_id:
        spot_expression += cell_expressions[i]
```

This aggregated spot expression serves as the training target during model training.

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:439-444]()

#### Embedding Extraction

For each patch, two types of embeddings are computed:

1. **Spot Embedding**: Full patch processed through PFM using `get_spot_embs()` [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:43-58]()
2. **Cell Embeddings**: Previously computed embeddings retrieved from `cell_dict` [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:460-466]()

These are stacked and saved as a single `.npy` file:

```python
patch_embeddings = [spot_embeddings.astype(np.float16)]  # First row: spot
for cell_id in cell_ids:
    emb = cell_dict[cell_id]['cell_embedding']
    patch_embeddings.append(emb.astype(np.float16))      # Subsequent rows: cells
patch_embeddings = np.vstack(patch_embeddings)
np.save(f'{data_folder}/embeddings{dataset_variant}/{model_name}/{patch_barcode}.npy', 
        patch_embeddings)
```

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:456-468]()

## Output Format

### Embedding Files (.npy)

Each patch generates one `.npy` file at `embeddings{dataset_variant}/{model_name}/{patch_barcode}.npy`:

| Row Index | Content | Shape |
|-----------|---------|-------|
| 0 | Spot embedding (full patch) | `(feature_dim,)` |
| 1 | Cell 0 embedding | `(feature_dim,)` |
| 2 | Cell 1 embedding | `(feature_dim,)` |
| ... | ... | ... |
| N | Cell N-1 embedding | `(feature_dim,)` |

The array shape is `(1 + num_cells, feature_dim)` where `feature_dim` depends on the PFM (e.g., 1024 for Phikon v2).

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:458-468]()

### Expression Files (.h5)

Each sample generates one HDF5 file at `expressions{dataset_variant}/{sample_id}_expressions.h5`:

```mermaid
graph TB
    H5["HDF5 File<br/>{sample_id}_expressions.h5"]
    
    subgraph "Group: patch_barcode"
        ATTRS["Attributes:<br/>spot_diameter, patch_size, um_per_px"]
        SPOT_EXPR["Dataset: spot_expression<br/>shape (num_genes,)"]
        CELL_EXPR["Dataset: cell_expressions<br/>shape (num_cells, num_genes)"]
        CELL_IDS["Dataset: cell_ids<br/>tagged with '_in' or '_out'"]
        CENTROIDS["Dataset: cell_centroids<br/>normalized (x, y) coords"]
        BBOXS["Dataset: cell_bbxs<br/>normalized (minx, miny, maxx, maxy)"]
    end
    
    H5 --> ATTRS
    H5 --> SPOT_EXPR
    H5 --> CELL_EXPR
    H5 --> CELL_IDS
    H5 --> CENTROIDS
    H5 --> BBOXS
```

The HDF5 structure [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:475-487]():

| Group/Dataset | Data Type | Compression | Description |
|---------------|-----------|-------------|-------------|
| `{patch_barcode}/` | Group | - | One group per patch |
| `.attrs['spot_diameter']` | int | - | Spot diameter in pixels |
| `.attrs['patch_size']` | int | - | Patch size in pixels |
| `.attrs['um_per_px']` | float | - | Microns per pixel |
| `spot_expression` | float | gzip (level 4) | Aggregated spot-level expression `(num_genes,)` |
| `cell_expressions` | float | gzip (level 4) | Cell-level expressions `(num_cells, num_genes)` |
| `cell_ids` | string | - | Cell IDs with `_in`/`_out` tags |
| `cell_centroids` | float32 | gzip (level 4) | Normalized centroids `(num_cells, 2)` |
| `cell_bbxs` | float32 | gzip (level 4) | Normalized bounding boxes `(num_cells, 4)` |

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:474-487]()

## Spatial Filtering and Quality Control

The pipeline implements multiple levels of spatial filtering to ensure data quality:

### Tissue Mask Creation

The `create_tissue_mask()` function [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:113-162]() builds a tissue mask from GeoJSON polygons with robust error handling:

1. **Geometry Validation**: Each polygon is validated and fixed using `buffer(0)` if invalid
2. **Union Operation**: Multiple tissue polygons are combined using `unary_union()` with fallback to iterative union if the operation fails
3. **Error Recovery**: Invalid polygons are skipped with warnings

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:113-162]()

### Cell Filtering

Cells are filtered at multiple stages [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:238-327]():

| Filter Stage | Condition | Purpose |
|--------------|-----------|---------|
| Transcript quality | `qv > qv_thr` | Remove low-quality transcript detections |
| Zero expression | `sum(gene_expression) > 0` | Remove cells with no detected transcripts |
| Invalid geometry | `cell_shape.is_valid` | Remove cells with malformed polygons |
| Tissue boundary | `tissue_mask.contains(centroid)` | Remove cells outside tissue |

### Patch Filtering

Patches are filtered to focus on tissue regions [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:340-454]():

| Filter | Condition | Impact |
|--------|-----------|--------|
| Tissue centroid | `tissue_mask.contains(patch_center)` | Skip patches outside tissue |
| No cells | `len(nearby_cells) == 0` | Skip empty patches |
| Zero expression | `len(cell_expressions) == 0` | Skip patches with no valid cells |

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:207-215](), [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:253-275](), [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:358-437]()

## Performance Optimization

The pipeline includes several optimizations for processing large WSIs:

### Batching Strategy

- **Cell batching**: Cells are accumulated and processed in batches (default: 32 GPU, 8 CPU) [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:306-316]()
- **Automatic batch sizing**: GPU batch size scales with VRAM (32 per 14GB) [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:514-520]()
- **Memory management**: Cell embeddings are deleted from `cell_dict` after being saved to reduce memory [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:465-466]()

### Spatial Optimization

- **Search radius**: Only cells within `search_radius` of patch center are considered [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:362-367]()
- **Bounds check**: Quick bbox intersection check before expensive geometry operations [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:395-398]()

### Progress Tracking

The pipeline prints progress every 10,000 cells and 1,000 patches with ETA estimates:

```
Processed 10000/200000 cells (5.0%) - ETA: 0:5:30/1:45:00
Processed 1000/10000 patches (10.0%) - ETA: 0:2:15/0:18:30
```

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:241-246](), [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:344-349]()

The script reads sample IDs from the configuration:

```yaml
data:
  lung:
    train:
      dataset_ids:
        - SAMPLE_ID_1
        - SAMPLE_ID_2
    ood:
      dataset_ids:
        - SAMPLE_ID_3
```

All samples from both `train` and `ood` splits are processed unless `--indices` is specified.

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:495-536]()

## Helper Functions

### crop_tile()

Extracts a square image region from a PyVips image:

```python
def crop_tile(image, x_pixel, y_pixel, spot_diameter):
    spot = image.crop(x_pixel, y_pixel, spot_diameter, spot_diameter)
    main_tile = np.ndarray(buffer=spot.write_to_memory(),
                           dtype=format_to_dtype[spot.format],
                           shape=[spot.height, spot.width, spot.bands])
    return main_tile[:, :, :3]  # Return only RGB channels
```

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:87-93]()

### fix_invalid_geometry()

Attempts to repair invalid Shapely geometries:

```python
def fix_invalid_geometry(geom):
    if not geom.is_valid:
        fixed = geom.buffer(0)  # Standard fix
        if fixed.is_valid:
            return fixed
        # Fallback to make_valid() if available
    return geom
```

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:96-110]()

### sort_genes_by_variability()

Loads or generates a gene ordering for consistent indexing:

- Loads from `{data_folder}/{ordered_genes_file}` if exists
- Otherwise calls `order_genes()` from utils to generate new ordering
- Returns list of gene names in order of decreasing variability

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:61-84]()

# Page: Data Preprocessing and Normalization

# Data Preprocessing and Normalization

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [deepspot2cell/dataloader.py](deepspot2cell/dataloader.py)
- [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py](deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py)

</details>



This document describes the data preprocessing and normalization strategies implemented in DeepSpot2Cell. These transformations are applied to gene expression data before it is fed into the model during training and inference. For information about the overall dataset creation process, see [Dataset Creation](#5.1). For details about the data loading pipeline, see [DS2CDataset and Data Loading](#4.2).

## Purpose and Scope

DeepSpot2Cell implements a multi-stage normalization pipeline that standardizes gene expression data across different scales (spot-level and cell-level) to enable effective model training. The normalization process handles:

- **Library size normalization**: Accounting for varying sequencing depths across spots and cells
- **Log transformation**: Stabilizing variance in count data
- **Standard scaling (z-score normalization)**: Centering and scaling features to unit variance
- **Min-max scaling**: Normalizing features to a [0, 1] range
- **Separate normalization for spots vs. cells**: Different statistics for aggregated spot data versus individual cell data

All preprocessing is performed by the `DS2CDataset` class during data loading and can be configured via constructor parameters.

---

## Normalization Pipeline Overview

The following diagram illustrates the complete normalization pipeline from raw counts to model-ready tensors:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Data"
        RAW_SPOT["Raw Spot Counts<br/>(aggregated 55μm region)"]
        RAW_CELLS["Raw Cell Counts<br/>(individual cells)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 1: Library Normalization"
        SPOT_LIB["Spot Library Normalization<br/>norm_counts * expr / sum"]
        CELL_LIB["Cell Library Normalization<br/>norm_counts * expr / inspot_total"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 2: Log Transformation"
        LOG["Log1p Transform<br/>np.log1p(normalized_data)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 3: Optional Standard Scaling"
        SPOT_SCALER["Spot StandardScaler<br/>spot_scaler.transform()"]
        CELL_SCALER["Cell StandardScaler<br/>cell_scaler.transform()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 4: Optional Min-Max Scaling"
        SPOT_MINMAX["Spot Min-Max<br/>(data - spot_gene_min) / spot_gene_range"]
        CELL_MINMAX["Cell Min-Max<br/>(data - cell_gene_min) / cell_gene_range"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        SPOT_OUT["Normalized Spot Expression<br/>torch.tensor"]
        CELL_OUT["Normalized Cell Expressions<br/>torch.tensor"]
    end
    
    RAW_SPOT --> SPOT_LIB
    RAW_CELLS --> CELL_LIB
    
    SPOT_LIB --> LOG
    CELL_LIB --> LOG
    
    LOG --> SPOT_SCALER
    LOG --> CELL_SCALER
    
    SPOT_SCALER --> SPOT_MINMAX
    CELL_SCALER --> CELL_MINMAX
    
    SPOT_MINMAX --> SPOT_OUT
    CELL_MINMAX --> CELL_OUT
```

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataloader.py:280-319]()

---

## DS2CDataset Preprocessing Components

The `DS2CDataset` class manages all preprocessing functionality. The following diagram shows the key components and their relationships:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "DS2CDataset Class"
        INIT["__init__()<br/>Initialize parameters"]
        
        subgraph "Normalization Parameters"
            NORMALIZE["normalize: bool"]
            NORM_COUNTS["norm_counts: float<br/>(default 1e4)"]
            STD_SCALE["standard_scaling: bool"]
            MINMAX["minmax: bool"]
        end
        
        subgraph "Computed Statistics"
            SPOT_SCALER["spot_scaler:<br/>StandardScaler"]
            CELL_SCALER["cell_scaler:<br/>StandardScaler"]
            SPOT_MIN["spot_gene_min:<br/>np.ndarray"]
            SPOT_MAX["spot_gene_max:<br/>np.ndarray"]
            CELL_MIN["cell_gene_min:<br/>np.ndarray"]
            CELL_MAX["cell_gene_max:<br/>np.ndarray"]
        end
        
        subgraph "Core Methods"
            COMPUTE_STATS["_compute_dataset_statistics()<br/>Fit scalers & compute min/max"]
            PREPROCESS["preprocess()<br/>Apply transformations"]
            INVERSE["inverse_transform()<br/>Reverse transformations"]
        end
    end
    
    INIT --> NORMALIZE
    INIT --> NORM_COUNTS
    INIT --> STD_SCALE
    INIT --> MINMAX
    
    NORMALIZE --> COMPUTE_STATS
    STD_SCALE --> COMPUTE_STATS
    MINMAX --> COMPUTE_STATS
    
    COMPUTE_STATS --> SPOT_SCALER
    COMPUTE_STATS --> CELL_SCALER
    COMPUTE_STATS --> SPOT_MIN
    COMPUTE_STATS --> SPOT_MAX
    COMPUTE_STATS --> CELL_MIN
    COMPUTE_STATS --> CELL_MAX
    
    SPOT_SCALER --> PREPROCESS
    CELL_SCALER --> PREPROCESS
    SPOT_MIN --> PREPROCESS
    SPOT_MAX --> PREPROCESS
    CELL_MIN --> PREPROCESS
    CELL_MAX --> PREPROCESS
    
    PREPROCESS --> INVERSE
```

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataloader.py:9-36](), [deepspot2cell/dataloader.py:37-144]()

---

## Library Size Normalization

Library size normalization accounts for varying sequencing depths across different spots and cells. This is the first and most critical normalization step.

### Spot-Level Normalization

For spot-level expression data, each spot is normalized independently:

```python
norm_counts * spot_expression / sum(spot_expression)
```

This ensures that each spot's total counts sum to `norm_counts` (typically 10,000), making expression levels comparable across spots with different sequencing depths.

### Cell-Level Normalization

Cell-level normalization is more complex because cells are normalized relative to their parent spot's total:

```python
# Calculate total counts from cells inside the spot
inspot_total = sum(cell_sums[cells_inside_spot])

# Normalize all cells (inside and outside) by this total
norm_cells = norm_counts * cell_expressions / inspot_total
```

This approach has two important properties:
1. **Consistency**: The sum of normalized cell expressions within a spot approximately equals the normalized spot expression
2. **Handling outside cells**: Cells outside the spot boundary (marked with `_out` suffix) are normalized using the same `inspot_total`, maintaining relative scale

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataloader.py:280-294]()

---

## Log Transformation

After library normalization, a log1p transformation is applied to stabilize variance:

```python
log_data = np.log1p(norm_data)
```

The `log1p` function computes `log(1 + x)`, which:
- Handles zero counts gracefully (log(1 + 0) = 0)
- Reduces the impact of highly expressed genes
- Makes the data distribution more approximately normal

This transformation is always applied when `normalize=True` and occurs before any subsequent scaling operations.

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataloader.py:296]()

---

## Standard Scaling (Z-Score Normalization)

When `standard_scaling=True`, the dataset computes separate `StandardScaler` objects for spots and cells during initialization.

### Computing Scalers

The `_compute_dataset_statistics` method collects all log-normalized expressions and fits separate scalers:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Training Data Collection"
        SPOTS["All Spot<br/>Log Expressions"]
        CELLS["All Cell<br/>Log Expressions<br/>(nonzero only)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Scaler Fitting"
        FIT_SPOT["StandardScaler.fit()<br/>→ spot_scaler"]
        FIT_CELL["StandardScaler.fit()<br/>→ cell_scaler"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Statistics Stored"
        SPOT_MEAN["spot_scaler.mean_"]
        SPOT_STD["spot_scaler.scale_"]
        CELL_MEAN["cell_scaler.mean_"]
        CELL_STD["cell_scaler.scale_"]
    end
    
    SPOTS --> FIT_SPOT
    CELLS --> FIT_CELL
    
    FIT_SPOT --> SPOT_MEAN
    FIT_SPOT --> SPOT_STD
    FIT_CELL --> CELL_MEAN
    FIT_CELL --> CELL_STD
```

The standard scaling transformation is:

```python
scaled_data = (log_data - mean) / std
```

This centers each gene at zero mean with unit variance, making genes with different expression ranges comparable.

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataloader.py:55-124](), [deepspot2cell/dataloader.py:298-311]()

### Separate Spot and Cell Scalers

A critical design decision is maintaining separate scalers for spots versus cells:

| Aspect | Spot Scaler | Cell Scaler |
|--------|-------------|-------------|
| **Training Data** | All spot expressions from dataset | All non-zero cell expressions from dataset |
| **Mean Range** | Typically higher (aggregated signal) | Typically lower (single-cell signal) |
| **Application** | Applied to spot targets during training | Applied to cell features and predictions |
| **Purpose** | Normalize aggregated 55μm region data | Normalize individual cell data |

This separation is necessary because:
- Spots represent aggregated signals from ~10-30 cells
- Cells have sparser, lower-magnitude expression patterns
- Using the same scaler would distort the relative magnitudes

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataloader.py:110-124](), [deepspot2cell/dataloader.py:304-311]()

---

## Min-Max Scaling

When `minmax=True`, an additional min-max normalization scales data to [0, 1]:

```python
scaled_data = (log_data - gene_min) / gene_range
```

where `gene_range = gene_max - gene_min`.

### Computing Min-Max Statistics

During `_compute_dataset_statistics`, the dataset tracks per-gene minimum and maximum values separately for spots and cells:

| Statistic | Spot Values | Cell Values |
|-----------|-------------|-------------|
| `spot_gene_min` | Minimum log-normalized value per gene across all spots | - |
| `spot_gene_max` | Maximum log-normalized value per gene across all spots | - |
| `cell_gene_min` | - | Minimum log-normalized value per gene across all nonzero cells |
| `cell_gene_max` | - | Maximum log-normalized value per gene across all nonzero cells |

The range is computed with a safeguard against zero division:

```python
gene_range = gene_max - gene_min
gene_range[gene_range < 1e-8] = 1.0  # Avoid division by zero
```

Min-max scaling is applied after standard scaling (if enabled) and provides bounded output values useful for certain model architectures.

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataloader.py:45-144](), [deepspot2cell/dataloader.py:313-318]()

---

## Data Flow Through Preprocessing

The following diagram traces a single data sample through the complete preprocessing pipeline:

```mermaid
graph TB
    START["__getitem__(idx)<br/>Load sample from HDF5"]
    
    LOAD["Load from expression_data:<br/>- spot_expression<br/>- cell_expressions<br/>- cell_ids"]
    
    CHECK_ZERO["Check spot_sum > 0<br/>Skip if zero"]
    
    FILTER_CELLS["Filter nonzero cells:<br/>nonzero_mask = cell_expressions.sum(axis=1) > 0"]
    
    LOAD_EMB["Load embeddings:<br/>patch_embeddings[0] → spot<br/>patch_embeddings[1:][nonzero_mask] → cells"]
    
    NORMALIZE{"normalize=True?"}
    
    PREPROCESS_SPOT["preprocess(spot_expression,<br/>is_spot=True)"]
    PREPROCESS_CELLS["preprocess(cell_expressions,<br/>is_spot=False,<br/>inspot_mask=is_inside_spot)"]
    
    PAD["Pad to max_cells:<br/>padded_embeds[0:num_cells] = cell_embeddings<br/>padded_exprs[0:num_cells] = cell_expressions"]
    
    TENSOR["Convert to torch.tensor:<br/>patch_embedding, cell_embeddings,<br/>spot_expression, cell_expressions,<br/>cell_mask, is_inside_spot"]
    
    RETURN["Return batch dict"]
    
    START --> LOAD
    LOAD --> CHECK_ZERO
    CHECK_ZERO --> FILTER_CELLS
    FILTER_CELLS --> LOAD_EMB
    LOAD_EMB --> NORMALIZE
    
    NORMALIZE -->|Yes| PREPROCESS_SPOT
    NORMALIZE -->|Yes| PREPROCESS_CELLS
    NORMALIZE -->|No| PAD
    
    PREPROCESS_SPOT --> PAD
    PREPROCESS_CELLS --> PAD
    
    PAD --> TENSOR
    TENSOR --> RETURN
```

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataloader.py:164-270]()

---

## Inverse Transformation

The `inverse_transform` method reverses the normalization pipeline, converting model predictions back to log-space:

```mermaid
graph LR
    INPUT["Scaled Predictions<br/>(from model)"]
    
    MINMAX_INV{"minmax enabled?"}
    MINMAX_REVERSE["data * gene_range + gene_min"]
    
    STD_INV{"standard_scaling<br/>enabled?"}
    STD_REVERSE["scaler.inverse_transform(data)"]
    
    OUTPUT["Log-space<br/>Expression Values"]
    
    INPUT --> MINMAX_INV
    MINMAX_INV -->|Yes| MINMAX_REVERSE
    MINMAX_INV -->|No| STD_INV
    MINMAX_REVERSE --> STD_INV
    
    STD_INV -->|Yes| STD_REVERSE
    STD_INV -->|No| OUTPUT
    STD_REVERSE --> OUTPUT
```

The inverse transform is applied in reverse order:
1. **Undo min-max scaling** (if enabled): `data = data * gene_range + gene_min`
2. **Undo standard scaling** (if enabled): `data = scaler.inverse_transform(data)`

Note that the log transformation is **not reversed** by this method. To obtain raw counts, additional steps would be needed:
```python
# After inverse_transform, data is in log-space
raw_counts = np.expm1(log_data) * total_counts / norm_counts
```

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataloader.py:321-348]()

---

## Configuration Parameters

The following table summarizes all normalization-related parameters accepted by `DS2CDataset.__init__`:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `normalize` | `bool` | `True` | Enable library normalization and log transformation |
| `norm_counts` | `float` | `1e4` | Target total counts for library normalization |
| `standard_scaling` | `bool` | `False` | Enable z-score normalization using `StandardScaler` |
| `minmax` | `bool` | `False` | Enable min-max scaling to [0, 1] range |

These parameters are typically set via the training configuration YAML file. See [Training Configuration](#6.2) for details on how to configure these values.

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataloader.py:10]()

---

## Optional Spatial Smoothing and Augmentation

In addition to the core normalization pipeline, `utils_dataloader.py` provides functions for optional data augmentation:

### Spatial Smoothing

The `spatial_upsample_and_smooth` function can smooth expression values using k-nearest neighbors in latent space:

```python
if smooth_n > 0:
    neigh = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=smooth_n)
    neigh.fit(adata.obsm["latent"])
    neigh_idx = neigh.kneighbors(adata.obsm["latent"], return_distance=False)
    smooth_counts = adata.X[neigh_idx].mean(axis=1)
```

This averages expression values across `smooth_n` neighbors, reducing noise.

### Clustering-Based Balancing

The function also supports clustering-based balanced sampling:

| Method | Description | Function |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| `default` | PCA + Leiden clustering | `run_default(adata, resolution)` |
| `aestetik` | AESTETIK multi-modal clustering | `run_aestetik(adata, window_size, resolution)` |

After clustering, samples are balanced by oversampling underrepresented clusters:
```python
n_count = np.max(adata.obs.label.value_counts())
resampled_barcodes = get_balanced_index(sample_barcode, adata.obs.leiden, n_count)
```

**Note:** These augmentation functions are provided for advanced use cases but are not used in the default DeepSpot2Cell training pipeline.

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:20-98]()

---

## Normalization Statistics Logging

During dataset initialization, `_compute_dataset_statistics` prints detailed statistics about the normalization:

```python
print(f"Max cells per patch: {max_cells}")
print(f"Mean cells per patch: {avg_cells}")
print(f"Mean cells per spot: {np.mean(cells_per_spot):.2f}")

if standard_scaling:
    print(f"Fit Spot StandardScaler on {all_spot_log_expressions.shape[0]} spot expressions")
    print(f"Spot Mean: min={spot_scaler.mean_.min():.4f}, max={spot_scaler.mean_.max():.4f}")
    print(f"Spot Std: min={spot_scaler.scale_.min():.4f}, max={spot_scaler.scale_.max():.4f}")
```

These logs are useful for verifying that:
- The dataset loaded correctly
- Normalization statistics are reasonable
- Separate spot/cell scalers have different parameters (as expected)

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataloader.py:126-144]()

---

## Summary

The DeepSpot2Cell preprocessing pipeline implements a sophisticated multi-stage normalization strategy:

1. **Library normalization** ensures comparable expression magnitudes across samples with different sequencing depths
2. **Log transformation** stabilizes variance and handles zero counts
3. **Standard scaling** (optional) centers and scales features to unit variance
4. **Min-max scaling** (optional) bounds features to [0, 1]
5. **Separate normalization** for spots vs. cells maintains appropriate relative scales
6. **Inverse transformation** allows converting model predictions back to log-space

All preprocessing is handled automatically by the `DS2CDataset` class during data loading, with behavior controlled by constructor parameters. The design ensures that spot-level supervision signals remain properly scaled relative to cell-level features during training, enabling the model to learn the resolution transfer from spot-supervised training to cell-level predictions.

---

# Configuration

<details>

## Purpose and Scope

This page provides an overview of DeepSpot2Cell's configuration system, which uses YAML files to control all aspects of dataset processing and model training. The configuration system centralizes parameter management and enables reproducible experiments by explicitly defining all settings in version-controlled files.

For detailed documentation of specific configuration parameters:
- Dataset configuration parameters: see [Dataset Configuration](#6.1)
- Training configuration parameters: see [Training Configuration](#6.2)

For information about how configuration is used during execution:
- Dataset creation workflow: see [Dataset Creation](#5.1)
- Training workflow: see [Training Script](#8.1)

---

## Configuration System Architecture

DeepSpot2Cell uses a two-tier configuration system that separates concerns between data preparation and model training:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Configuration Files"
        DATASET_CONFIG["configs/dataset.example.yaml<br/>Dataset Configuration"]
        TRAINING_CONFIG["configs/training.example.yaml<br/>Training Configuration"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Processing Stage"
        DATASET_SCRIPT["dataset_creation.py<br/>process_sample()"]
        DATASET_CONFIG --> DATASET_SCRIPT
    end
    
    subgraph "Training Stage"
        TRAIN_SCRIPT["scripts/train.py<br/>main()"]
        TRAINING_CONFIG --> TRAIN_SCRIPT
    end
    
    subgraph "Generated Artifacts"
        EMBEDDINGS["Morphology Embeddings<br/>.npy files"]
        EXPRESSIONS["Expression Data<br/>.h5 files"]
        MODEL_CHECKPOINTS["Trained Models<br/>.pt checkpoints"]
    end
    
    DATASET_SCRIPT --> EMBEDDINGS
    DATASET_SCRIPT --> EXPRESSIONS
    EMBEDDINGS --> TRAIN_SCRIPT
    EXPRESSIONS --> TRAIN_SCRIPT
    TRAIN_SCRIPT --> MODEL_CHECKPOINTS
```

**Diagram: Configuration System Flow**

The system enforces a clean separation: dataset configuration controls the one-time preprocessing phase where morphological features are extracted and saved, while training configuration controls the iterative training process that can be repeated with different hyperparameters without re-preprocessing data.

**Sources:** [configs/dataset.example.yaml](), [configs/training.example.yaml]()

---

## Configuration File Types

DeepSpot2Cell provides two distinct configuration file types:

| Configuration Type | File Pattern | Purpose | Used By | Frequency |
|-------------------|--------------|---------|---------|-----------|
| Dataset | `dataset.*.yaml` | Controls data preprocessing, PFM selection, spatial parameters | `dataset_creation.py` | Once per dataset |
| Training | `training.*.yaml` | Controls model architecture, training hyperparameters, optimization | `scripts/train.py` | Multiple times during experimentation |

### File Locations

All configuration files reside in the `configs/` directory at the repository root:

```
configs/
├── dataset.example.yaml     # Example dataset configuration
└── training.example.yaml    # Example training configuration
```

Users create their own configuration files by copying these examples and modifying paths and parameters for their specific use case.

**Sources:** [configs/dataset.example.yaml](), [configs/training.example.yaml]()

---

**Diagram: Dataset Configuration Structure**

The dataset configuration has two main sections:
- **`data`**: Defines input paths, PFM selection, spatial dimensions, and sample organization by tissue type
- **`processing`**: Controls batch sizes for GPU and CPU operations during embedding computation

**Diagram: Training Configuration Structure**

The training configuration has five main sections:
- **`experiment`**: Identifies the experiment and sets reproducibility parameters
- **`data`**: Specifies data locations, train/val splits, and preprocessing options
- **`dataloader`**: Controls PyTorch DataLoader behavior
- **`model`**: Defines model architecture and optimization hyperparameters
- **`trainer`**: Configures PyTorch Lightning Trainer settings including early stopping

**Sources:** [configs/training.example.yaml:1-54]()

## Configuration Loading Mechanism

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Configuration Loading"
        YAML_FILE["YAML File<br/>dataset.yaml or training.yaml"]
        YAML_PARSER["yaml.safe_load()"]
        CONFIG_DICT["Configuration Dictionary<br/>Nested Python dict"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Usage in Dataset Creation"
        DS_MAIN["dataset_creation.py<br/>main()"]
        DS_ARGS["argparse<br/>--config argument"]
        DS_CONFIG["Config dict accessed<br/>config['data']['model_name']<br/>config['processing']['gpu_batch_size']"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Usage in Training"
        TR_MAIN["scripts/train.py<br/>main()"]
        TR_ARGS["argparse<br/>--config argument"]
        UTILS_LOAD["utils.utils.load_config()"]
        TR_CONFIG["Config object<br/>config.data.train_ids<br/>config.model.lr"]
    end
    
    YAML_FILE --> YAML_PARSER
    YAML_PARSER --> CONFIG_DICT
    
    DS_ARGS --> DS_MAIN
    CONFIG_DICT --> DS_MAIN
    DS_MAIN --> DS_CONFIG
    
    TR_ARGS --> TR_MAIN
    CONFIG_DICT --> UTILS_LOAD
    UTILS_LOAD --> TR_CONFIG
    TR_MAIN --> TR_CONFIG
```

**Diagram: Configuration Loading Code Entities**

Configuration files are loaded through standard Python YAML parsing:

1. **Dataset creation** loads configuration directly as a dictionary and accesses values using bracket notation (e.g., `config['data']['model_name']`)

2. **Training script** uses a utility function `load_config()` from `deepspot2cell.utils.utils` that provides dot-notation access to configuration values (e.g., `config.model.lr`)

Both approaches read the same YAML format but provide different access patterns to suit their respective use cases.

**Sources:** [configs/dataset.example.yaml](), [configs/training.example.yaml]()

---

## Configuration Workflow

The two configuration types are used at different stages of the DeepSpot2Cell pipeline:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant DatasetYAML as dataset.yaml
    participant DatasetScript as dataset_creation.py
    participant TrainingYAML as training.yaml
    participant TrainScript as scripts/train.py
    participant Model as DeepSpot2Cell Model
    
    User->>DatasetYAML: 1. Configure preprocessing<br/>(PFM, paths, samples)
    User->>DatasetScript: 2. Run preprocessing
    DatasetScript->>DatasetYAML: Load config
    DatasetScript->>DatasetScript: Extract embeddings
    DatasetScript-->>User: Generates .npy and .h5 files
    
    Note over User,TrainingYAML: Preprocessing complete, now configure training
    
    User->>TrainingYAML: 3. Configure training<br/>(hyperparams, data splits)
    User->>TrainScript: 4. Run training
    TrainScript->>TrainingYAML: Load config
    TrainScript->>Model: Instantiate with config.model.*
    TrainScript->>TrainScript: Train using config.trainer.*
    TrainScript-->>User: Generates .pt checkpoint
    
    Note over User,Model: Can iterate training with new configs<br/>without re-preprocessing
```

**Diagram: Configuration Usage Sequence**

The separation between dataset and training configuration enables efficient experimentation:
- Dataset configuration is used once to generate preprocessed artifacts
- Training configuration can be modified and reused multiple times without re-running expensive preprocessing
- Each configuration file is self-contained and version-controllable for reproducibility

**Sources:** [configs/dataset.example.yaml](), [configs/training.example.yaml]()

## Configuration Parameter Categories

The table below categorizes configuration parameters by their functional purpose:

| Category | Parameters | Configuration File | Purpose |
|----------|-----------|-------------------|---------|
| **Paths** | `data_folder`, `model_path` | Both | Locate input data and model weights |
| **Identifiers** | `dataset_variant`, `model_name`, `experiment.name` | Both | Version and identify artifacts |
| **Spatial Geometry** | `spot_diameter_px`, `patch_size_px`, `neighb_degree` | Dataset, Training | Define spatial scales and relationships |
| **Data Selection** | `train_ids`, `val_ids`, `ordered_genes_file`, `qv_thr` | Both | Select samples, genes, and quality thresholds |
| **Preprocessing** | `normalize`, `standard_scaling`, `minmax`, `norm_counts` | Training | Transform expression values |
| **Model Architecture** | `n_ensemble`, `phi2rho_size`, `dropout` | Training | Define network structure |
| **Optimization** | `lr`, `weight_decay`, `batch_size` | Training | Control learning process |
| **Training Control** | `max_epochs`, `early_stopping`, `gradient_clip_val` | Training | Manage training duration and stability |
| **Compute Resources** | `gpu_batch_size`, `cpu_batch_size`, `devices`, `num_workers` | Both | Allocate computational resources |
| **Reproducibility** | `random_seed` | Training | Ensure deterministic results |

**Sources:** [configs/dataset.example.yaml:1-27](), [configs/training.example.yaml:1-54]()

---

## Configuration Best Practices

When creating configuration files for your experiments:

1. **Copy from examples**: Start with `dataset.example.yaml` or `training.example.yaml` and modify for your needs

2. **Use absolute paths**: Always specify absolute paths for `data_folder` and `model_path` to avoid ambiguity

3. **Match configurations**: Ensure `data_folder`, `dataset_variant`, and `model_name` match between dataset and training configs so training can find preprocessed data

4. **Version your configs**: Include configurations in version control alongside code for full reproducibility

5. **Document experiments**: Use descriptive `experiment.name` values to identify different training runs

6. **Set seeds consistently**: Use the same `random_seed` value across related experiments for reproducibility

7. **Start conservative**: Use provided default values for hyperparameters, then tune systematically

8. **Enable early stopping**: Set `early_stopping.enabled: true` to prevent overfitting during initial experiments

**Sources:** [configs/dataset.example.yaml](), [configs/training.example.yaml]()

---

## Integration with Pipeline Components

Configuration parameters flow through the DeepSpot2Cell pipeline to control different components:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Configuration Files"
        DS_CONFIG["dataset.yaml"]
        TR_CONFIG["training.yaml"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Processing Layer"
        PFM_LOADER["PFM Model Loading<br/>Uses: model_name, model_path"]
        TILE_EXTRACT["Tile Extraction<br/>Uses: spot_diameter_px, patch_size_px"]
        SAMPLE_FILTER["Sample Selection<br/>Uses: train_ids, ood_ids"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Dataset Layer"
        DS2C_DATASET["DS2CDataset<br/>Uses: normalize, standard_scaling<br/>neighb_degree, load_cell_types"]
        DATALOADER["DataLoader<br/>Uses: batch_size, num_workers"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Layer"
        MODEL_INIT["DeepSpot2Cell.__init__()<br/>Uses: n_ensemble, phi2rho_size<br/>dropout, cell_gt_available"]
        OPTIMIZER["configure_optimizers()<br/>Uses: lr, weight_decay"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Training Layer"
        TRAINER["PyTorch Lightning Trainer<br/>Uses: max_epochs, accelerator<br/>devices, precision"]
        CALLBACKS["Callbacks<br/>Uses: early_stopping.*"]
    end
    
    DS_CONFIG --> PFM_LOADER
    DS_CONFIG --> TILE_EXTRACT
    DS_CONFIG --> SAMPLE_FILTER
    
    TR_CONFIG --> DS2C_DATASET
    TR_CONFIG --> DATALOADER
    TR_CONFIG --> MODEL_INIT
    TR_CONFIG --> OPTIMIZER
    TR_CONFIG --> TRAINER
    TR_CONFIG --> CALLBACKS
    
    PFM_LOADER --> TILE_EXTRACT
    TILE_EXTRACT --> SAMPLE_FILTER
    SAMPLE_FILTER --> DS2C_DATASET
    DS2C_DATASET --> DATALOADER
    DATALOADER --> MODEL_INIT
    MODEL_INIT --> OPTIMIZER
    OPTIMIZER --> TRAINER
    TRAINER --> CALLBACKS
```

**Diagram: Configuration Parameter Flow to Code Components**

Configuration parameters are consumed by specific classes and functions throughout the pipeline:

- **Dataset creation** uses spatial parameters to extract appropriately sized image tiles
- **DS2CDataset** uses preprocessing flags to normalize expression data
- **DeepSpot2Cell** model initialization uses architecture parameters
- **PyTorch Lightning Trainer** uses training control parameters

This modular consumption pattern allows each component to access only the configuration values it needs.

**Sources:** [configs/dataset.example.yaml](), [configs/training.example.yaml]()
