# Page: Dataset Configuration

# Dataset Configuration

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [configs/dataset.example.yaml](configs/dataset.example.yaml)
- [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py](deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py)

</details>



This page documents the configuration parameters used to control dataset creation and preprocessing in DeepSpot2Cell. The dataset configuration file defines how raw HEST-1k data is processed into training-ready embeddings and expression files.

For information about training configuration parameters, see [Training Configuration](#6.2). For details on the dataset creation process itself, see [Dataset Creation](#5.1).

## Overview

Dataset configuration is specified in YAML files (typically `configs/dataset.example.yaml`). These configurations control:

- **Data paths** and file locations for HEST-1k data
- **Pathology Foundation Model (PFM)** selection and loading
- **Spatial dimensions** for tile extraction (spots, patches, cells)
- **Quality filtering** thresholds for transcript selection
- **Dataset organization** including train/test splits per tissue type
- **Processing parameters** for batch sizes during embedding computation

The configuration is loaded by `dataset_creation.py` to preprocess samples, extract tiles, compute PFM embeddings, and generate the `.h5` expression files and `.npy` embedding files required for training.

**Sources:** [configs/dataset.example.yaml:1-27](), [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:495-511]()

## Configuration File Structure

```mermaid
graph TB
    CONFIG["dataset.example.yaml"]
    
    subgraph "data Section"
        PATHS["Path Configuration<br/>data_folder, model_path"]
        MODELS["Model Selection<br/>model_name"]
        SPATIAL["Spatial Dimensions<br/>spot_diameter_px, patch_size_px"]
        QUALITY["Quality Thresholds<br/>qv_thr"]
        TISSUE["Tissue-Specific Config<br/>lung, breast, etc."]
    end
    
    subgraph "processing Section"
        BATCH["Batch Sizes<br/>gpu_batch_size, cpu_batch_size"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Tissue-Specific Configuration"
        GENES["Gene Lists<br/>ordered_genes_file"]
        SPLITS["Dataset Splits<br/>train.dataset_ids, ood.dataset_ids"]
    end
    
    CONFIG --> PATHS
    CONFIG --> MODELS
    CONFIG --> SPATIAL
    CONFIG --> QUALITY
    CONFIG --> TISSUE
    CONFIG --> BATCH
    
    TISSUE --> GENES
    TISSUE --> SPLITS
```

**Sources:** [configs/dataset.example.yaml:1-27]()

## Data Section Parameters

### Basic Paths and Identifiers

| Parameter | Type | Description | Example |
|-----------|------|-------------|---------|
| `data_folder` | string | Absolute path to HEST data directory containing subdirectories (`wsis/`, `metadata/`, `tissue_seg/`, etc.) | `/absolute/path/to/hest_data` |
| `dataset_variant` | string | Suffix appended to output directories (`embeddings{variant}/`, `expressions{variant}/`) to version datasets | `_v1` |

These parameters define the root data location and allow multiple dataset versions to coexist.

**Sources:** [configs/dataset.example.yaml:1-3](), [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:166-167]()

### Model Selection

| Parameter | Type | Description | Example |
|-----------|------|-------------|---------|
| `model_name` | string | Name of the Pathology Foundation Model to use for feature extraction | `phikonv2`, `uni`, `hoptimus0` |
| `model_path` | string | Absolute path to the PFM checkpoint or model directory | `/absolute/path/to/phikonv2` |

The `model_name` determines which PFM architecture is loaded, while `model_path` specifies where to find the model weights. These are passed to `get_morphology_model_and_preprocess()` to instantiate the feature extractor.

**Sources:** [configs/dataset.example.yaml:4-5](), [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:506-507, 526]()

### Spatial Dimensions

DeepSpot2Cell supports two methods for specifying spatial dimensions: **pixel-based** or **micron-based**.

**Pixel-Based Configuration (Recommended):**

| Parameter | Type | Description | Example |
|-----------|------|-------------|---------|
| `spot_diameter_px` | int | Diameter of each spot in pixels (typically 160px for 55μm spots at ~0.34μm/px) | `160` |
| `patch_size_px` | int | Size of square patches extracted from the WSI in pixels | `224` |

**Micron-Based Configuration (Alternative):**

| Parameter | Type | Description | Example |
|-----------|------|-------------|---------|
| `spot_diameter` | float | Diameter of each spot in microns | `55.0` |
| `patch_size` | float | Size of square patches in microns | `110.0` |

When using micron-based configuration, dimensions are converted to pixels using the `pixel_size_um_estimated` metadata field for each sample (default: 0.2125 μm/px).

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Configuration Input"
        CONFIG_PX["spot_diameter_px: 160<br/>patch_size_px: 224"]
        CONFIG_UM["spot_diameter: 55.0<br/>patch_size: 110.0"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Pixel Calculation"
        METADATA["metadata.json<br/>pixel_size_um_estimated"]
        CALC["Conversion:<br/>px = um / um_per_px"]
    end
    
    subgraph "dataset_creation.py Usage"
        READ["load_config()"]
        CHECK{"spot_diameter_px<br/>exists?"}
        USE_PX["Use pixel values"]
        USE_UM["Calculate from microns"]
        RESULT["spot_diameter (px)<br/>patch_size (px)"]
    end
    
    CONFIG_PX --> READ
    CONFIG_UM --> READ
    READ --> CHECK
    CHECK -->|Yes| USE_PX
    CHECK -->|No| USE_UM
    USE_UM --> METADATA
    METADATA --> CALC
    CALC --> RESULT
    USE_PX --> RESULT
```

**Sources:** [configs/dataset.example.yaml:7-12](), [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:176-183]()

### Quality Thresholds

| Parameter | Type | Description | Default |
|-----------|------|-------------|---------|
| `qv_thr` | int | Quality value threshold for filtering Xenium transcripts. Transcripts with `qv <= qv_thr` are excluded. | `20` |

This parameter controls transcript quality filtering. In the HEST-1k dataset, each transcript has a quality value (`qv`) indicating detection confidence. Setting a higher threshold removes lower-quality transcripts but reduces transcript count.

**Sources:** [configs/dataset.example.yaml:14](), [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:210-214]()

### Tissue-Specific Configuration

Each tissue type (e.g., `lung`, `breast`) has its own configuration block specifying gene ordering and dataset splits.

```yaml
lung:
  ordered_genes_file: lung_ordered_genes.json
  train:
    dataset_ids:
      - SAMPLE_ID_1
      - SAMPLE_ID_2
  ood:
    dataset_ids: []
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `ordered_genes_file` | string | Filename (relative to `data_folder`) containing ordered list of gene names to use for this tissue type |
| `train.dataset_ids` | list[string] | List of HEST sample IDs to process for training |
| `ood.dataset_ids` | list[string] | List of HEST sample IDs to process for out-of-distribution evaluation |

The `ordered_genes_file` defines the fixed gene ordering used to create expression vectors. All samples in a tissue type must use the same gene order for consistency. If the file doesn't exist, it's generated automatically by ranking genes by variability across samples.

**Sources:** [configs/dataset.example.yaml:15-22](), [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:61-84, 509]()

## Processing Section Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description | Default |
|-----------|------|-------------|---------|
| `gpu_batch_size` | int | Number of image tiles to process in parallel when using GPU | `32` (auto-computed based on VRAM) |
| `cpu_batch_size` | int | Number of image tiles to process in parallel when using CPU | `8` |

These parameters control the batch size for PFM feature extraction. The GPU batch size is automatically calculated based on available VRAM if not specified (approximately `VRAM_GB * 32 / 14`). Larger batch sizes improve throughput but require more memory.

**Sources:** [configs/dataset.example.yaml:24-26](), [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:514-524]()

## Configuration Parameter Reference

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "config.yaml Parameters"
        DATA_FOLDER["data_folder"]
        VARIANT["dataset_variant"]
        MODEL_NAME["model_name"]
        MODEL_PATH["model_path"]
        SPOT_PX["spot_diameter_px"]
        PATCH_PX["patch_size_px"]
        QV_THR["qv_thr"]
        GENES_FILE["ordered_genes_file"]
        TRAIN_IDS["train.dataset_ids"]
        GPU_BATCH["gpu_batch_size"]
    end
    
    subgraph "dataset_creation.py Usage"
        LOAD_CFG["load_config(args.config)"]
        GET_SAMPLES["sample_ids = config['data'][dataset]['train']['dataset_ids']"]
        GET_MODEL["get_morphology_model_and_preprocess(model_name, device, model_path)"]
        GET_DIMS["if config['data'].get('spot_diameter_px'):<br/>    spot_diameter = config['data']['spot_diameter_px']<br/>else:<br/>    spot_diameter = int(config['data']['spot_diameter'] / um_per_px)"]
        FILTER_TX["filtered_df = filtered_df[filtered_df['qv'] > qv_thr]"]
        SORT_GENES["sort_genes_by_variability(adata, config)"]
        SET_BATCH["batch_size = processing_cfg.get('gpu_batch_size', auto_batch)"]
        SAVE_PATHS["f'{data_folder}/embeddings{dataset_variant}/{model_name}/{patch_barcode}.npy'<br/>f'{data_folder}/expressions{dataset_variant}/{sample_id}_expressions.h5'"]
    end
    
    DATA_FOLDER --> LOAD_CFG
    VARIANT --> SAVE_PATHS
    MODEL_NAME --> GET_MODEL
    MODEL_PATH --> GET_MODEL
    SPOT_PX --> GET_DIMS
    PATCH_PX --> GET_DIMS
    QV_THR --> FILTER_TX
    GENES_FILE --> SORT_GENES
    TRAIN_IDS --> GET_SAMPLES
    GPU_BATCH --> SET_BATCH
    
    LOAD_CFG --> GET_SAMPLES
    LOAD_CFG --> GET_MODEL
    LOAD_CFG --> GET_DIMS
    LOAD_CFG --> FILTER_TX
    LOAD_CFG --> SORT_GENES
    LOAD_CFG --> SET_BATCH
    LOAD_CFG --> SAVE_PATHS
```

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:503-535]()

## Usage in Dataset Creation Pipeline

The dataset configuration flows through the `dataset_creation.py` script as follows:

1. **Configuration Loading** [`dataset_creation.py:503`](): The script loads the YAML configuration file specified via `--config` argument
2. **Sample Selection** [`dataset_creation.py:509`](): Sample IDs are extracted from the tissue-specific configuration (combining `train.dataset_ids` and `ood.dataset_ids`)
3. **Model Initialization** [`dataset_creation.py:526-527`](): The PFM is loaded using `model_name` and `model_path`
4. **Batch Size Configuration** [`dataset_creation.py:514-524`](): Batch size is set based on available hardware and configuration
5. **Per-Sample Processing** [`dataset_creation.py:533-535`](): For each sample:
   - Spatial dimensions are computed [`dataset_creation.py:177-183`]()
   - Gene ordering is loaded/created [`dataset_creation.py:61-84`]()
   - Transcripts are filtered by quality [`dataset_creation.py:210-214`]()
   - Cell and spot embeddings are computed and saved to `embeddings{variant}/{model_name}/`
   - Expression data is saved to `expressions{variant}/{sample_id}_expressions.h5`

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant CLI as Command Line
    participant DC as dataset_creation.py
    participant CFG as Config YAML
    participant HEST as HEST Data
    participant PFM as Pathology Foundation Model
    participant OUT as Output Files
    
    CLI->>DC: python dataset_creation.py --config dataset.yaml --dataset lung
    DC->>CFG: load_config()
    CFG-->>DC: config dict
    
    DC->>CFG: config['data']['lung']['train']['dataset_ids']
    CFG-->>DC: sample_ids list
    
    DC->>CFG: config['data']['model_name'], config['data']['model_path']
    CFG-->>DC: model_name, model_path
    DC->>PFM: get_morphology_model_and_preprocess(model_name, model_path)
    PFM-->>DC: model, preprocess
    
    loop For each sample_id
        DC->>HEST: iter_hest(data_folder, id_list=[sample_id])
        HEST-->>DC: st (spatial transcriptomics object)
        
        DC->>CFG: config['data']['spot_diameter_px'], config['data']['qv_thr']
        CFG-->>DC: spatial dims, quality threshold
        
        DC->>DC: process_sample(sample_id, st, model, preprocess, config)
        Note over DC: Filter transcripts by qv_thr<br/>Extract tiles at spot_diameter_px, patch_size_px<br/>Compute PFM embeddings<br/>Aggregate expressions
        
        DC->>OUT: {data_folder}/embeddings{variant}/{model_name}/{patch_barcode}.npy
        DC->>OUT: {data_folder}/expressions{variant}/{sample_id}_expressions.h5
    end
```

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:495-535]()

## Complete Parameter Mapping

The following table shows how each configuration parameter maps to code usage:

| Config Path | Code Reference | Purpose |
|-------------|----------------|---------|
| `data.data_folder` | [`dataset_creation.py:166`]() | Base directory for all HEST data and outputs |
| `data.dataset_variant` | [`dataset_creation.py:167`]() | Suffix for `embeddings{variant}/` and `expressions{variant}/` directories |
| `data.model_name` | [`dataset_creation.py:506, 526`]() | PFM architecture name passed to `get_morphology_model_and_preprocess()` |
| `data.model_path` | [`dataset_creation.py:507, 526`]() | Path to PFM checkpoint passed to `get_morphology_model_and_preprocess()` |
| `data.spot_diameter_px` | [`dataset_creation.py:178`]() | Pixel diameter of spots (used if specified) |
| `data.patch_size_px` | [`dataset_creation.py:179`]() | Pixel size of square patches (used if specified) |
| `data.spot_diameter` | [`dataset_creation.py:181`]() | Micron diameter of spots (converted to pixels) |
| `data.patch_size` | [`dataset_creation.py:182`]() | Micron size of patches (converted to pixels) |
| `data.qv_thr` | [`dataset_creation.py:210, 213`]() | Quality value threshold for filtering transcripts |
| `data.{tissue}.ordered_genes_file` | [`dataset_creation.py:62-72`]() | JSON file with ordered gene list for expression vectors |
| `data.{tissue}.train.dataset_ids` | [`dataset_creation.py:509`]() | HEST sample IDs to process for training |
| `data.{tissue}.ood.dataset_ids` | [`dataset_creation.py:509`]() | HEST sample IDs to process for OOD evaluation |
| `processing.gpu_batch_size` | [`dataset_creation.py:518`]() | Batch size for GPU feature extraction |
| `processing.cpu_batch_size` | [`dataset_creation.py:522`]() | Batch size for CPU feature extraction |

**Sources:** [configs/dataset.example.yaml:1-27](), [deepspot2cell/dataset_creation.py:1-536]()

## Example Configuration

A complete example configuration for processing lung tissue samples with Phikon v2:

```yaml
data:
  data_folder: /data/hest_data
  dataset_variant: _v1
  model_name: phikonv2
  model_path: /models/phikonv2
  
  # Pixel-based dimensions
  spot_diameter_px: 160
  patch_size_px: 224
  
  qv_thr: 20
  
  lung:
    ordered_genes_file: lung_ordered_genes.json
    train:
      dataset_ids:
        - TENX95_lung
        - TENX97_lung
        - ZEN38_lung
    ood:
      dataset_ids:
        - TENX101_lung

processing:
  gpu_batch_size: 32
  cpu_batch_size: 8
```

This configuration will:
- Process 3 training samples and 1 OOD sample from HEST-1k lung data
- Use Phikon v2 for feature extraction
- Extract 224×224 pixel patches centered on 160-pixel diameter spots
- Filter transcripts with quality value > 20
- Save outputs to `/data/hest_data/embeddings_v1/phikonv2/` and `/data/hest_data/expressions_v1/`
- Use batch size 32 on GPU for feature extraction

**Sources:** [configs/dataset.example.yaml:1-27]()

# Page: Training Configuration

# Training Configuration

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [configs/training.example.yaml](configs/training.example.yaml)
- [scripts/train.py](scripts/train.py)

</details>



This page documents the training configuration system used to control DeepSpot2Cell model training. Training configuration is specified via YAML files that define experiment settings, data preprocessing options, dataloader parameters, model hyperparameters, and trainer settings including early stopping. 

For information about dataset creation configuration (preprocessing parameters for generating embeddings and expression files), see [Dataset Configuration](#6.1). For the actual training script implementation, see [Training Script](#8.1).

## Purpose and Scope

The training configuration system provides a declarative interface for controlling all aspects of model training without modifying code. Configuration files are YAML-formatted and organize parameters into five main sections: `experiment`, `data`, `dataloader`, `model`, and `trainer`. The configuration is loaded by the training script and used to instantiate datasets, dataloaders, models, and PyTorch Lightning trainers.

## Configuration File Structure

The training configuration file follows a hierarchical structure with five top-level sections:

```mermaid
graph TB
    CONFIG["training.yaml<br/>Configuration File"]
    
    EXPERIMENT["experiment:<br/>Experiment metadata"]
    DATA["data:<br/>Data loading & preprocessing"]
    DATALOADER["dataloader:<br/>DataLoader parameters"]
    MODEL["model:<br/>Model hyperparameters"]
    TRAINER["trainer:<br/>Training loop settings"]
    
    CONFIG --> EXPERIMENT
    CONFIG --> DATA
    CONFIG --> DATALOADER
    CONFIG --> MODEL
    CONFIG --> TRAINER
    
    EXPERIMENT --> EXP_NAME["name: Experiment identifier"]
    EXPERIMENT --> EXP_SEED["random_seed: Reproducibility"]
    
    DATA --> DATA_FOLDER["data_folder: Root path"]
    DATA --> DATA_IDS["train_ids, val_ids: Sample splits"]
    DATA --> DATA_NORM["normalize, standard_scaling, minmax"]
    DATA --> DATA_NEIGHB["neighb_degree: Context spots"]
    
    DATALOADER --> DL_BATCH["batch_size: Batch size"]
    DATALOADER --> DL_WORKERS["num_workers: Data loading threads"]
    
    MODEL --> MODEL_LR["lr: Learning rate"]
    MODEL --> MODEL_WD["weight_decay: L2 regularization"]
    MODEL --> MODEL_DROP["dropout: Dropout probability"]
    MODEL --> MODEL_ENS["n_ensemble: Ensemble size"]
    MODEL --> MODEL_PHI2RHO["phi2rho_size: Bottleneck dimension"]
    
    TRAINER --> TRAINER_EPOCHS["max_epochs: Training duration"]
    TRAINER --> TRAINER_ACC["accelerator, devices: Hardware"]
    TRAINER --> TRAINER_ES["early_stopping: Early stopping config"]
```

**Sources:** [configs/training.example.yaml:1-54]()

## Configuration Sections

### Experiment Settings

The `experiment` section defines metadata and reproducibility settings for the training run.

| Parameter | Type | Description | Default |
|-----------|------|-------------|---------|
| `name` | string | Experiment identifier used for output directory naming | Required |
| `random_seed` | integer | Random seed for reproducibility across PyTorch, NumPy, and Python | Required |

**Example:**
```yaml
experiment:
  name: ds2c_baseline
  random_seed: 2024
```

The `random_seed` is passed to `fix_seed()` to ensure deterministic behavior across all random number generators.

**Sources:** [configs/training.example.yaml:1-3](), [scripts/train.py:168]()

### Data Configuration

The `data` section specifies data paths, sample splits, and preprocessing options. This section overlaps with dataset configuration but focuses on training-time settings.

| Parameter | Type | Description | Default |
|-----------|------|-------------|---------|
| `data_folder` | string | Absolute path to data root directory | Required |
| `dataset_variant` | string | Dataset variant suffix (e.g., `_v1`) | Required |
| `model_name` | string | PFM identifier (e.g., `phikonv2`, `uni`, `hoptimus0`) | Required |
| `train_ids` | list[string] | Sample IDs for training set | Required |
| `val_ids` | list[string] | Sample IDs for validation set | `[]` |
| `normalize` | boolean | Apply library size normalization | `true` |
| `standard_scaling` | boolean | Apply standard scaling (z-score) | `false` |
| `minmax` | boolean | Apply min-max scaling to [0, 1] | `false` |
| `norm_counts` | integer | Target library size for normalization | `10000` |
| `neighb_degree` | integer | Number of neighboring spot rings to load | `1` |
| `load_cell_types` | boolean | Load cell type annotations if available | `false` |
| `scellst` | boolean | Use single-cell spatial transcriptomics mode | `false` |

**Example:**
```yaml
data:
  data_folder: /absolute/path/to/data_root
  dataset_variant: _v1
  model_name: phikonv2
  
  train_ids:
    - SAMPLE_ID_1
    - SAMPLE_ID_2
  val_ids:
    - SAMPLE_ID_VAL
  
  normalize: true
  standard_scaling: false
  minmax: false
  norm_counts: 10000
  neighb_degree: 1
  load_cell_types: false
  scellst: false
```

These parameters are passed directly to `DS2CDataset` constructors. Scaling statistics (means, standard deviations, min/max values) are computed on the training set and shared with the validation set to prevent data leakage.

**Sources:** [configs/training.example.yaml:5-22](), [scripts/train.py:20-60]()

### Dataloader Parameters

The `dataloader` section controls PyTorch DataLoader behavior.

| Parameter | Type | Description | Default |
|-----------|------|-------------|---------|
| `batch_size` | integer | Number of samples per batch | `4` |
| `num_workers` | integer | Number of worker processes for data loading | `4` |

**Example:**
```yaml
dataloader:
  batch_size: 4
  num_workers: 4
```

Additional DataLoader settings (shuffling, pin_memory) are hardcoded in the training script: training data is always shuffled, validation data is not shuffled, and `pin_memory` is enabled when CUDA is available.

**Sources:** [configs/training.example.yaml:24-26](), [scripts/train.py:63-87]()

### Model Hyperparameters

The `model` section defines hyperparameters for the DeepSpot2Cell architecture.

| Parameter | Type | Description | Default |
|-----------|------|-------------|---------|
| `lr` | float | Learning rate for Adam optimizer | `1e-4` |
| `weight_decay` | float | L2 regularization coefficient | `1e-6` |
| `dropout` | float | Dropout probability (used for both Phi and Rho if not separately specified) | `0.3` |
| `n_ensemble` | integer | Number of ensemble members (used for both Phi and Rho if not separately specified) | `8` |
| `phi2rho_size` | integer | Dimensionality of bottleneck layer between Phi and Rho ensembles | `512` |
| `cell_gt_available` | boolean | Whether cell-level ground truth is available (affects loss computation) | `true` |
| `p_phi` | float | Dropout probability for Phi ensemble (overrides `dropout`) | `null` |
| `p_rho` | float | Dropout probability for Rho ensemble (overrides `dropout`) | `null` |
| `n_ensemble_phi` | integer | Number of Phi ensemble members (overrides `n_ensemble`) | `null` |
| `n_ensemble_rho` | integer | Number of Rho ensemble members (overrides `n_ensemble`) | `null` |

**Example:**
```yaml
model:
  lr: 1.0e-4
  weight_decay: 1.0e-6
  dropout: 0.3
  n_ensemble: 8
  phi2rho_size: 512
  cell_gt_available: true
  # Optional: separate control for Phi and Rho
  # p_phi: 0.3
  # p_rho: 0.3
  # n_ensemble_phi: 8
  # n_ensemble_rho: 8
```

The `input_size` and `output_size` are automatically inferred from the dataset's embedding and expression dimensions, respectively. The model uses these hyperparameters to construct Phi and Rho ensemble modules.

**Sources:** [configs/training.example.yaml:28-38](), [scripts/train.py:90-110]()

### Trainer Settings

The `trainer` section configures the PyTorch Lightning Trainer and training loop behavior.

| Parameter | Type | Description | Default |
|-----------|------|-------------|---------|
| `max_epochs` | integer | Maximum number of training epochs | `50` |
| `accelerator` | string | Hardware accelerator (`auto`, `cpu`, `gpu`, `tpu`, `mps`) | `auto` |
| `devices` | integer/list | Number or list of devices to use | `1` |
| `precision` | integer/string | Floating point precision (`32`, `16`, `bf16`) | `32` |
| `gradient_clip_val` | float | Max gradient norm for clipping (`null` disables) | `null` |
| `log_every_n_steps` | integer | Logging frequency in steps | `50` |

**Example:**
```yaml
trainer:
  max_epochs: 50
  accelerator: auto
  devices: 1
  precision: 32
  gradient_clip_val: null
  log_every_n_steps: 50
```

#### Early Stopping Configuration

Early stopping is configured as a nested dictionary within the `trainer` section:

| Parameter | Type | Description | Default |
|-----------|------|-------------|---------|
| `enabled` | boolean | Whether to enable early stopping | `false` |
| `monitor` | string | Metric to monitor (`val_loss`, `val_pearson`, etc.) | `val_loss` |
| `patience` | integer | Number of epochs with no improvement before stopping | `5` |
| `mode` | string | Whether to minimize or maximize the metric (`min`, `max`) | `min` |
| `min_delta` | float | Minimum change to qualify as improvement | `0.001` |

**Example:**
```yaml
trainer:
  early_stopping:
    enabled: true
    monitor: val_loss
    patience: 5
    mode: min
    min_delta: 0.001
```

When enabled, an `EarlyStopping` callback is added to the trainer. The same `monitor` metric is used for model checkpointing to save the best model.

**Sources:** [configs/training.example.yaml:40-53](), [scripts/train.py:113-152]()

The configuration file is loaded and processed by the training script through several functions that map YAML sections to code entities.

### Configuration Loading Implementation

The `load_config()` function reads the YAML file and returns a dictionary:

```yaml
# Usage in train.py
cfg = load_config(cfg_path)
experiment_name = cfg["experiment"]["name"]
fix_seed(cfg["experiment"]["random_seed"])
```

Each build function extracts its relevant configuration section:

- `build_datasets()` extracts `cfg["data"]` and creates `DS2CDataset` instances for training and validation
- `build_dataloaders()` extracts `cfg["dataloader"]` and wraps datasets in PyTorch DataLoaders
- `build_model()` extracts `cfg["model"]` and instantiates `DeepSpot2Cell`
- `build_trainer()` extracts `cfg["trainer"]` and creates a PyTorch Lightning Trainer with callbacks

**Sources:** [scripts/train.py:15-17](), [scripts/train.py:162-175]()

**Sources:** [scripts/train.py:46-58]()

## Callbacks and Logging

The training script automatically configures two types of callbacks:

### Early Stopping Callback

When `trainer.early_stopping.enabled` is `true`, an `EarlyStopping` callback is created:

```python
EarlyStopping(
    monitor=early_cfg.get("monitor", "val_loss"),
    patience=early_cfg.get("patience", 5),
    mode=early_cfg.get("mode", "min"),
    min_delta=early_cfg.get("min_delta", 0.0),
)
```

### Model Checkpoint Callback

A `ModelCheckpoint` callback is always created to save the best model:

```python
ModelCheckpoint(
    dirpath=ckpt_dir,
    save_top_k=1,
    monitor=early_cfg.get("monitor", "val_loss"),
    mode=early_cfg.get("mode", "min"),
    filename="best-{epoch}-{val_loss:.4f}",
    auto_insert_metric_name=False,
)
```

Checkpoints are saved to `{output_dir}/checkpoints/` with the filename format `best-{epoch}-{val_loss:.4f}.ckpt`.

### CSV Logger

Training and validation metrics are logged to CSV files using PyTorch Lightning's `CSVLogger`:

```python
CSVLogger(save_dir=output_dir, name="logs")
```

Logs are saved to `{output_dir}/logs/version_0/metrics.csv`.

**Sources:** [scripts/train.py:113-152]()

## Example Configuration

A complete example configuration demonstrating typical settings:

```yaml
experiment:
  name: ds2c_baseline
  random_seed: 2024

data:
  data_folder: /path/to/data
  dataset_variant: _v1
  model_name: phikonv2
  
  train_ids:
    - TENX52
    - TENX53
  val_ids:
    - TENX54
  
  normalize: true
  standard_scaling: false
  minmax: false
  norm_counts: 10000
  neighb_degree: 1
  load_cell_types: false
  scellst: false

dataloader:
  batch_size: 4
  num_workers: 4

model:
  lr: 1.0e-4
  weight_decay: 1.0e-6
  dropout: 0.3
  n_ensemble: 8
  phi2rho_size: 512
  cell_gt_available: true

trainer:
  max_epochs: 50
  accelerator: auto
  devices: 1
  precision: 32
  gradient_clip_val: null
  log_every_n_steps: 50
  
  early_stopping:
    enabled: true
    monitor: val_loss
    patience: 5
    mode: min
    min_delta: 0.001
```

This configuration trains a DeepSpot2Cell model with 8-member ensembles, using library size normalization on the expression data, with a batch size of 4 and early stopping based on validation loss.

**Sources:** [configs/training.example.yaml:1-54]()

# Utility Modules

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [deepspot2cell/utils/__init__.py](deepspot2cell/utils/__init__.py)
- [deepspot2cell/utils/utils.py](deepspot2cell/utils/utils.py)
- [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py](deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py)
- [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py](deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py)

</details>



This document provides an overview of the utility modules in the `deepspot2cell.utils` package. These modules contain helper functions and supporting infrastructure that enable the core components of DeepSpot2Cell to function. The utilities are organized into three categories: image processing, data loading, and general utilities.

For detailed documentation of specific utility functions, see:
- Image processing utilities: [Image Processing Utilities](#7.1)
- Data loading utilities: [Data Loading Utilities](#7.2)
- General utilities: [General Utilities](#7.3)

For API reference documentation, see [deepspot2cell.utils Package](#9.2).

## Package Structure

The `deepspot2cell.utils` package consists of four files that together provide supporting functionality for data preprocessing, model training, and inference.


**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/__init__.py:1-3]()

## Module Categories

The utility modules are organized by functionality:

| Module | Purpose | Key Functions | Primary Users |
|--------|---------|---------------|---------------|
| `utils.py` | Configuration management, reproducibility, gene ordering | `load_config()`, `fix_seed()`, `order_genes()`, `model_fine_tune()`, `run_inference_from_dataloader()` | Training scripts, dataset creation |
| `utils_image.py` | PFM loading, image processing, tile extraction, inference | `get_morphology_model_and_preprocess()`, `crop_tile()`, `predict_spot2cell_from_image_paths()` | Dataset creation, inference workflows |
| `utils_dataloader.py` | Data augmentation, spatial processing, clustering | `spatial_upsample_and_smooth()`, `run_default()`, `run_aestetik()`, `load_data()` | Data loading, preprocessing |

## Image Processing Utilities

The `utils_image.py` module provides functions for loading pathology foundation models, processing histology images, and running inference on image data. Key capabilities include:

- **PFM Model Loading**: Support for UNI, H-optimus-0, Phikon v1, Phikon v2, InceptionV3, ResNet50, and DenseNet121
- **Image Tile Extraction**: Functions to crop specific regions from whole slide images using PyVips
- **Inference Workflows**: Prediction functions for spot-level and cell-level transcriptomics

```mermaid

    end

        PRED_DS2C["predict_spot2cell_from_image_paths()"]
        PREDICTIONS["Gene Expression<br/>Predictions"]
    end
    
    MODEL_NAME --> GET_MODEL
```

### Supported Pathology Foundation Models

The following table shows the PFM models supported by `get_morphology_model_and_preprocess()`:

| Model Name | Architecture | Feature Dimension | Normalization | Use Case |
|------------|-------------|-------------------|---------------|----------|
| `uni` | ViT-Large/16 | 1024 | ImageNet stats | UNI foundation model |
| `hoptimus0` | ViT-giant/14 (DINOv2) | 1536 | Custom H&E stats | H-optimus-0 |
| `phikon` | ViT | 768 | HuggingFace processor | Phikon v1 |
| `phikonv2` | ViT | 1024 | HuggingFace processor | Phikon v2 |
| `inception` | InceptionV3 | 2048 | ImageNet weights | Baseline |
| `resnet50` | ResNet-50 | 2048 | ImageNet weights | Baseline |
| `densenet121` | DenseNet-121 | 1024 | ImageNet weights | Baseline |

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py:36-182]()

## Data Loading Utilities

The `utils_dataloader.py` module provides functions for data augmentation, spatial processing, and clustering. These utilities are primarily used during dataset creation and training to enhance data quality and balance.

Key functionalities:

- **Spatial Clustering**: `run_default()` and `run_aestetik()` for Leiden clustering with spatial context
- **Data Augmentation**: `spatial_upsample_and_smooth()` for balancing and smoothing spot-level data
- **Balanced Sampling**: `get_balanced_index()` for creating balanced datasets across clusters
- **Data Loading**: `load_data()` and `load_multiple_pickles()` for loading preprocessed data

```mermaid

    end
    
    subgraph "Spatial Processing"
        INPUT["Input Data<br/>counts, coordinates"]
        SPATIAL_UP["spatial_upsample_and_smooth()"]
        BALANCED["get_balanced_index()"]
        SMOOTH["KNN Smoothing"]
        OUTPUT["Balanced &<br/>Smoothed Data"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Loading"
        PICKLE_FILES["*.pkl files"]
        LOAD_MULTI["load_multiple_pickles()"]
        LOAD_DATA["load_data()"]
        NORMALIZED["Normalized<br/>Expression Data"]
    end
    
    ADATA --> RUN_DEFAULT
    ADATA --> RUN_AESTETIK
    RUN_DEFAULT --> CLUSTERED
    RUN_AESTETIK --> CLUSTERED

```

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:20-99](), [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:124-175]()

### Clustering Configurations

The `spatial_upsample_and_smooth()` function supports two clustering methods:

| Method | Implementation | Parameters | Description |
|--------|----------------|------------|-------------|
| `default` | `run_default()` | `resolution` | Standard PCA + Leiden clustering with neighborhood graph |
| `aestetik` | `run_aestetik()` | `resolution`, `window_size` | AESTETIK framework with spatial awareness and multimodal integration |

Both methods produce:
- `adata.obsm["latent"]`: Low-dimensional representation for downstream processing
- `adata.obs["label"]`: Cluster assignments for balanced sampling

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:29-63]()

The `utils.py` module contains general-purpose functions for configuration management, reproducibility, gene ordering, model fine-tuning, and inference.

### Function Descriptions

| Function | Purpose | Inputs | Outputs |
|----------|---------|--------|---------|
| `load_config()` | Load YAML configuration files | `config_path` (str) | Configuration dictionary |
| `fix_seed()` | Set random seeds for reproducibility | `seed` (int) | None (sets global state) |
| `order_genes()` | Rank genes by variability across samples | `config` (dict) | Ordered gene list (JSON file) |
| `model_fine_tune()` | Fine-tune specific model layers | `model`, `dataloader`, flags | Trained model |
| `run_inference_from_dataloader()` | Batch inference with dataloader | `model`, `dataloader`, `device` | Predictions array |
| `plot_loss_values()` | Visualize training progress | `train_losses`, `val_losses` | Matplotlib plot |

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils.py:75-200]()

## Public API Design

The `__init__.py` file exposes a carefully curated public API that balances convenience with clarity:

```python
# Selective imports from utils.py
from .utils import fix_seed, load_config, order_genes

# Selective imports from utils_image.py
from .utils_image import get_morphology_model_and_preprocess, format_to_dtype, predict_spot2cell_from_image_paths

# Wildcard import from utils_dataloader.py
from .utils_dataloader import *
```

This design has three patterns:

1. **Explicit Core Functions**: `fix_seed`, `load_config`, `order_genes` are explicitly imported because they're frequently used and form the core workflow
2. **Key Image Functions**: Essential image processing functions are explicitly exposed for inference workflows
3. **All Data Loading Functions**: The entire data loading module is exported via `*` because these functions are often used together in data preprocessing pipelines

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/__init__.py:1-3]()

## Common Usage Patterns

### Pattern 1: Dataset Creation Setup

```python
from deepspot2cell.utils import load_config, fix_seed, get_morphology_model_and_preprocess

# Load configuration
config = load_config('configs/dataset.yaml')

# Set reproducibility
fix_seed(config['seed'])

# Load PFM model
model, preprocess, feature_dim = get_morphology_model_and_preprocess(
    model_name=config['model_name'],
    device='cuda',
    model_path=config['model_path']
)
```

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils.py:106-109](), [deepspot2cell/utils/utils.py:92-100](), [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py:36-183]()

### Pattern 2: Training Configuration

```python
from deepspot2cell.utils import load_config, fix_seed

# Load training configuration
config = load_config('configs/training.yaml')

# Ensure reproducibility
fix_seed(42)
```

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils.py:92-109]()

### Pattern 3: Inference from Images

```python
from deepspot2cell.utils import get_morphology_model_and_preprocess, predict_spot2cell_from_image_paths

# Load models
morphology_model, preprocess, _ = get_morphology_model_and_preprocess('phikonv2', 'cuda', model_path)

# Predict from image paths
predictions = predict_spot2cell_from_image_paths(
    cell_image_path='cell.png',
    spot_image_path='spot.png',
    neighbor_image_paths=['neighbor1.png', 'neighbor2.png'],
    deepspot2cell_model=trained_model,
    morphology_model=morphology_model,
    preprocess=preprocess,
    device='cuda',
    gene_names=gene_list
)
```

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py:364-458]()

## Dependencies

The utility modules rely on several external libraries:

| Library | Used In | Purpose |
|---------|---------|---------|
| PyTorch | All modules | Tensor operations, model loading |
| PyVips | `utils_image.py` | Efficient whole slide image processing |
| Scanpy | `utils.py`, `utils_dataloader.py` | Single-cell analysis, clustering |
| scikit-learn | `utils_dataloader.py` | Nearest neighbors, scaling |
| timm | `utils_image.py` | Vision transformer models |
| transformers | `utils_image.py` | HuggingFace model loading |
| HEST | `utils.py` | HEST dataset iteration |
| Lightning | `utils.py` | Training utilities |
| AESTETIK | `utils_dataloader.py` | Spatial clustering (optional) |

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils.py:1-20](), [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py:1-19](), [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:1-17]()

# Page: Image Processing Utilities

# Image Processing Utilities

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py](deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the image processing utilities provided in `deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py`. These utilities handle three primary responsibilities:

1. **Pathology Foundation Model (PFM) Loading**: Loading and configuring different pre-trained vision models for feature extraction
2. **Image Tile Operations**: Extracting, cropping, and subdividing image patches from whole-slide images
3. **Inference Functions**: Applying trained models to predict gene expression from H&E image data

For data loading utilities (neighbor computation, augmentation, smoothing), see [Data Loading Utilities](#7.2). For general configuration and training utilities, see [General Utilities](#7.3).

Sources: [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py:1-458]()

---

## Pathology Foundation Model Loading

The `get_morphology_model_and_preprocess()` function loads pre-trained pathology foundation models and their corresponding preprocessing pipelines. This function supports multiple PFM architectures used in computational pathology.

### Supported Models

| Model Name | Architecture | Feature Dimension | Key Characteristics |
|------------|--------------|-------------------|---------------------|
| `uni` | ViT-Large/16 | 1024 | Mahmood Lab's pathology foundation model |
| `hoptimus0` | ViT-Giant/14 | 1536 | Bioptimus H-optimus-0 model |
| `phikon` | ViT-Base | 768 | Owkin's Phikon v1 model |
| `phikonv2` | ViT-Large | 1024 | Owkin's Phikon v2 model |
| `inception` | Inception-v3 | 2048 | Pre-trained ImageNet model |
| `resnet50` | ResNet-50 | 2048 | Pre-trained ImageNet model |
| `densenet121` | DenseNet-121 | 1024 | Pre-trained ImageNet model |

Sources: [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py:36-182]()

### Model Loading Workflow

```mermaid
graph TB
    INPUT["get_morphology_model_and_preprocess()<br/>model_name, device, model_path"]
    
    subgraph "Model Selection"
        UNI["uni<br/>timm.create_model('vit_large_patch16_224')"]
        HOPT["hoptimus0<br/>timm.create_model('vit_giant_patch14_reg4_dinov2')"]
        PHIK["phikon/phikonv2<br/>AutoModel.from_pretrained()"]
        LEGACY["inception/resnet50/densenet121<br/>torchvision.models"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Preprocessing Pipeline"
        PREPROC_UNI["transforms.Compose()<br/>Resize(224), Normalize<br/>mean=(0.485,0.456,0.406)"]
        PREPROC_HOPT["transforms.Compose()<br/>Resize(224), Normalize<br/>mean=(0.707,0.579,0.704)"]
        PREPROC_PHIK["AutoImageProcessor<br/>from_pretrained()"]
        PREPROC_LEGACY["weights.transforms()"]
    end
    
    OUTPUT["Returns:<br/>morphology_model<br/>preprocess function<br/>feature_dim"]
    
    INPUT --> UNI
    INPUT --> HOPT
    INPUT --> PHIK
    INPUT --> LEGACY
    
    UNI --> PREPROC_UNI
    HOPT --> PREPROC_HOPT
    PHIK --> PREPROC_PHIK
    LEGACY --> PREPROC_LEGACY
    
    PREPROC_UNI --> OUTPUT
    PREPROC_HOPT --> OUTPUT
    PREPROC_PHIK --> OUTPUT
    PREPROC_LEGACY --> OUTPUT
```

**Figure: PFM Loading and Preprocessing Pipeline**

Sources: [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py:36-182]()

### UNI Model Configuration

The UNI model uses a Vision Transformer architecture optimized for pathology images. It requires specific normalization parameters:

- **Architecture**: ViT-Large with 16x16 patches
- **Input Size**: 224x224 pixels
- **Normalization**: ImageNet statistics (mean=[0.485, 0.456, 0.406], std=[0.229, 0.224, 0.225])
- **Feature Dimension**: 1024
- **Model Loading**: Weights loaded from `model_path` using `torch.load()`

Sources: [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py:38-58]()

### H-optimus-0 Model Configuration

The H-optimus-0 model uses a larger Vision Transformer trained specifically on histopathology data:

- **Architecture**: ViT-Giant with 14x14 patches and DINOv2 registration
- **Input Size**: 224x224 pixels  
- **Normalization**: Pathology-specific statistics (mean=[0.707, 0.579, 0.704], std=[0.212, 0.230, 0.178])
- **Feature Dimension**: 1536
- **Dynamic Image Size**: Supports variable input dimensions

Sources: [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py:59-80]()

### Phikon v2 Model Configuration

Phikon v2 uses Hugging Face's transformers library with custom wrapper classes:

- **Architecture**: ViT-Large from transformers
- **Feature Dimension**: 1024
- **Preprocessing**: `AutoImageProcessor` from Hugging Face
- **Custom Wrapper**: `MyModel` class extracts the `[CLS]` token embedding
- **Forward Methods**: Supports both `forward()` and `forward_features()` for different use cases

Sources: [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py:107-135]()

---

## Image Tile Operations

These functions handle the geometric operations required to extract and process image patches from whole-slide images.

```mermaid
graph LR
    WSI["Whole Slide Image<br/>pyvips.Image"]
    
    subgraph "Tile Extraction Functions"
        GET_LOW["get_low_res_image()<br/>downsample_factor"]
        CROP["crop_tile()<br/>x_pixel, y_pixel, diameter"]
        COMPUTE["compute_mini_tiles()<br/>n_tiles, super_resolution"]
    end
    
    OUTPUT_LOW["Downsampled Image<br/>np.ndarray"]
    OUTPUT_CROP["Single Tile<br/>np.ndarray[H,W,3]"]
    OUTPUT_MINI["List of Sub-tiles<br/>List[np.ndarray]"]
    
    WSI --> GET_LOW
    WSI --> CROP
    
    GET_LOW --> OUTPUT_LOW
    CROP --> OUTPUT_CROP
    OUTPUT_CROP --> COMPUTE
    COMPUTE --> OUTPUT_MINI
```

**Figure: Image Tile Processing Operations**

Sources: [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py:185-239]()

### get_low_res_image()

Downsamples a whole-slide image for visualization or quick processing:

**Parameters**:
- `image_path` (str): Path to the image file
- `downsample_factor` (int): Factor by which to downsample the image

**Returns**: `np.ndarray` - Downsampled image array

**Implementation**: Uses `pyvips.Image.resize()` for memory-efficient downsampling of large images. The function automatically handles format conversion using the `format_to_dtype` mapping dictionary.

Sources: [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py:185-192](), [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py:22-33]()

### crop_tile()

Extracts a square tile centered at specified pixel coordinates:

**Parameters**:
- `image` (pyvips.Image): Source image object
- `x_pixel` (int): X-coordinate of tile center
- `y_pixel` (int): Y-coordinate of tile center  
- `cell_diameter` (int): Width and height of the tile in pixels

**Returns**: `np.ndarray` - RGB tile array with shape `[cell_diameter, cell_diameter, 3]`

**Implementation**: Centers the crop by offsetting by `cell_diameter // 2`, uses pyvips' efficient `crop()` method, and extracts only the first 3 channels (RGB).

Sources: [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py:195-203]()

### compute_mini_tiles()

Subdivides a tile into smaller sub-tiles for multi-resolution processing:

**Parameters**:
- `image` (np.ndarray): Input tile to subdivide
- `n_tiles` (int): Total number of sub-tiles (must be a perfect square, e.g., 4, 9, 16)
- `super_resolution_mode` (bool): If True, extracts only the center sub-tile

**Returns**: `List[np.ndarray]` - List of sub-tile arrays

**Algorithm**:
1. Compute grid dimensions: `n = sqrt(n_tiles)`
2. Calculate sub-tile size: `square_size = D // n`
3. Extract tiles in row-major order
4. In super-resolution mode, extract only the center tile with padding

**Use Case**: During training, spot tiles are subdivided into mini-tiles to provide finer-grained spatial information while maintaining computational efficiency.

Sources: [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py:206-239]()

---

## Prediction Functions

The utility module provides three prediction functions for different inference scenarios. Each function follows a similar pattern but differs in the spatial scale and input structure.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Spot-Level Prediction"
        SPOT_FUNC["predict_spot_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path()"]
        SPOT_INPUT["Inputs:<br/>image_path, adata<br/>spot_diameter, n_mini_tiles"]
        SPOT_TILE["Extracts:<br/>spot tile<br/>sub-tiles<br/>neighbor tiles"]
        SPOT_OUT["Output:<br/>spot-level expression<br/>np.ndarray[n_spots, n_genes]"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Cell-Level Prediction"
        CELL_FUNC["predict_cell_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path()"]
        CELL_INPUT["Inputs:<br/>image_path, adata<br/>cell_diameter, radius_neighbors"]
        CELL_TILE["Extracts:<br/>cell tile<br/>neighbor tiles"]
        CELL_OUT["Output:<br/>cell-level expression<br/>np.ndarray[n_cells, n_genes]"]
    end
    
    subgraph "DeepSpot2Cell Prediction"
        DS2C_FUNC["predict_spot2cell_from_image_paths()"]
        DS2C_INPUT["Inputs:<br/>cell_image_path<br/>spot_image_path<br/>neighbor_image_paths"]
        DS2C_EMB["Extracts embeddings<br/>from pre-cropped images"]
        DS2C_OUT["Output:<br/>gene expression dict<br/>Dict[gene_name, float]"]
    end
    
    SPOT_INPUT --> SPOT_FUNC
    SPOT_FUNC --> SPOT_TILE
    SPOT_TILE --> SPOT_OUT
    
    CELL_INPUT --> CELL_FUNC
    CELL_FUNC --> CELL_TILE
    CELL_TILE --> CELL_OUT
    
    DS2C_INPUT --> DS2C_FUNC
    DS2C_FUNC --> DS2C_EMB
    DS2C_EMB --> DS2C_OUT
```

**Figure: Prediction Function Hierarchy**

Sources: [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py:246-457]()

### predict_spot_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path()

Predicts spot-level gene expression from H&E images using spatial context.

**Function Signature**:
```python
predict_spot_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path(
    image_path,
    adata,
    spot_diameter,
    n_mini_tiles,
    preprocess,
    morphology_model,
    model_expression,
    device,
    super_resolution=False,
    neighbor_radius=1
)
```

**Parameters**:
- `image_path` (str): Path to the H&E image
- `adata` (AnnData): AnnData object containing spot coordinates in `.obs`
- `spot_diameter` (int): Diameter of spot tiles in pixels
- `n_mini_tiles` (int): Number of sub-tiles to extract from each spot
- `preprocess` (callable): Preprocessing function for the PFM
- `morphology_model` (nn.Module): Pre-trained PFM for feature extraction
- `model_expression` (nn.Module): Trained expression prediction model
- `device` (str): Device for computation ('cuda' or 'cpu')
- `super_resolution` (bool): Whether to use super-resolution mode
- `neighbor_radius` (int): Radius for neighbor spot identification

**Processing Pipeline**:
1. For each spot in `adata.obs`, compute neighboring spots using `compute_neighbors()`
2. Extract spot tile using `crop_tile()` centered at `(x_pixel, y_pixel)`
3. Subdivide spot tile into mini-tiles using `compute_mini_tiles()`
4. Extract neighbor spot tiles
5. Apply preprocessing and morphology model to all tiles
6. Convert embeddings using `detach_and_convert()`
7. Pass embeddings to `model_expression` for prediction
8. Apply inverse transform to convert predictions back to expression space

**Returns**: `np.ndarray` with shape `[n_spots, n_genes]`

Sources: [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py:246-297]()

### predict_cell_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path()

Predicts cell-level gene expression with spatial neighbor context.

**Function Signature**:
```python
predict_cell_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path(
    image_path,
    adata,
    cell_diameter,
    radius_neighbors,
    preprocess,
    morphology_model,
    model_expression,
    device
)
```

**Key Differences from Spot Prediction**:
- Uses `NearestNeighbors` from scikit-learn for radius-based neighbor finding
- Does not use mini-tiles (no sub-division of cell tiles)
- Simpler input structure: `[X_cell, X_neighbors]` vs `[X_spot, X_subspot, X_neighbors]`
- Designed for single-cell resolution data where each cell is individually identified

**Neighbor Computation**:
```python
neigh = NearestNeighbors(radius=radius_neighbors)
neigh.fit(adata.obs[["x_pixel", "y_pixel"]].values)
neighbors = neigh.radius_neighbors(..., return_distance=True, sort_results=True)[1]
neighbors = [n[1:] for n in neighbors]  # remove the cell itself
```

**Returns**: `np.ndarray` with shape `[n_cells, n_genes]`

Sources: [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py:300-361]()

### predict_spot2cell_from_image_paths()

DeepSpot2Cell-specific inference function for pre-extracted image tiles.

**Function Signature**:
```python
predict_spot2cell_from_image_paths(
    cell_image_path,
    spot_image_path,
    neighbor_image_paths,
    deepspot2cell_model,
    morphology_model,
    preprocess,
    device,
    gene_names=None
)
```

**Design Rationale**: This function is specifically designed for DeepSpot2Cell's training/inference paradigm where:
- Cell tiles are pre-extracted based on segmentation masks
- Spot tiles provide broader spatial context (55μm)
- Neighbor tiles provide multi-spot spatial relationships

**Key Features**:
1. **Pre-extracted Images**: Accepts paths to already-cropped tiles rather than extracting from WSI
2. **Helper Function**: Includes `extract_embedding()` nested function for consistent embedding extraction
3. **Missing Neighbor Handling**: Creates zero embeddings for missing neighbors
4. **Context Masking**: Generates boolean masks to indicate valid vs. padded embeddings
5. **Model-Specific API**: Calls `deepspot2cell_model._forward_single_cell()` directly

**Processing Flow**:

```mermaid
graph TB
    CELL_IMG["cell_image_path"]
    SPOT_IMG["spot_image_path"]
    NEIGH_IMG["neighbor_image_paths<br/>List[str]"]
    
    subgraph "Embedding Extraction"
        EXTRACT["extract_embedding()<br/>PIL.Image.open()<br/>preprocess()<br/>morphology_model()"]
    end
    
    CELL_EMB["cell_embedding<br/>torch.Tensor"]
    SPOT_EMB["spot_embedding<br/>torch.Tensor"]
    NEIGH_EMB["neighbor_embeddings<br/>List[torch.Tensor]"]
    
    CONTEXT["context = cat([spot] + neighbors)<br/>context_mask = [False, ...]"]
    
    MODEL["deepspot2cell_model._forward_single_cell(<br/>cell_embedding,<br/>context,<br/>context_mask)"]
    
    RESULTS["Dict[gene_name, float]"]
    
    CELL_IMG --> EXTRACT
    SPOT_IMG --> EXTRACT
    NEIGH_IMG --> EXTRACT
    
    EXTRACT --> CELL_EMB
    EXTRACT --> SPOT_EMB
    EXTRACT --> NEIGH_EMB
    
    SPOT_EMB --> CONTEXT
    NEIGH_EMB --> CONTEXT
    
    CELL_EMB --> MODEL
    CONTEXT --> MODEL
    
    MODEL --> RESULTS
```

**Figure: DeepSpot2Cell Prediction Workflow**

**Returns**: Dictionary mapping gene names to predicted expression values

Sources: [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py:364-457]()

## Utility Functions

### detach_and_convert()

Helper function to convert tensors to a consistent format for model input:

```python
def detach_and_convert(data):
    return data[None, ].detach().float()
```

Adds a batch dimension, detaches from computational graph, and converts to float32.

Sources: [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py:242-243]()

### format_to_dtype Dictionary

Mapping from pyvips image format strings to NumPy data types:

| Format | NumPy dtype |
|--------|-------------|
| `'uchar'` | `np.uint8` |
| `'ushort'` | `np.uint16` |
| `'float'` | `np.float32` |
| `'double'` | `np.float64` |

Used in `get_low_res_image()` and `crop_tile()` for format conversion.

Sources: [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py:22-33]()

## Common Usage Patterns

### Loading a PFM for Preprocessing

```python
from deepspot2cell.utils import get_morphology_model_and_preprocess

model, preprocess, feature_dim = get_morphology_model_and_preprocess(
    model_name="phikonv2",
    device="cuda",
    model_path="/path/to/phikon-v2"
)
```

### Extracting Tiles from WSI

```python
import pyvips

image = pyvips.Image.new_from_file("sample.tif")
cell_tile = crop_tile(image, x_pixel=1000, y_pixel=2000, cell_diameter=128)
mini_tiles = compute_mini_tiles(cell_tile, n_tiles=9)
```

### Running Spot-Level Prediction

```python
import scanpy as sc

adata = sc.read_h5ad("spatial_data.h5ad")
predictions = predict_spot_spatial_transcriptomics_from_image_path(
    image_path="tissue.tif",
    adata=adata,
    spot_diameter=256,
    n_mini_tiles=16,
    preprocess=preprocess,
    morphology_model=model,
    model_expression=trained_model,
    device="cuda",
    neighbor_radius=1
)
```

Sources: [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_image.py:36-297]()

# Page: Data Loading Utilities

# Data Loading Utilities

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [deepspot2cell/dataloader.py](deepspot2cell/dataloader.py)
- [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py](deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the utility functions in the `deepspot2cell.utils.utils_dataloader` module that support data loading, preprocessing, and augmentation operations. These utilities provide helper functions for spatial upsampling, smoothing, clustering, normalization, and balanced sampling.

For the core dataset class and main data loading pipeline, see [DS2CDataset and Data Loading](#4.2). For image processing utilities, see [Image Processing Utilities](#7.1). For general utilities like configuration loading and seed fixing, see [General Utilities](#7.3).

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:1-175]()

---

## Overview of Utility Functions

The `utils_dataloader` module provides a collection of independent helper functions organized into four main categories:

| Category | Functions | Purpose |
|----------|-----------|---------|
| **Spatial Processing** | `spatial_upsample_and_smooth`, `run_default`, `run_aestetik`, `get_balanced_index` | Spatial upsampling, clustering, and balanced sampling |
| **Normalization** | `log1p_normalization` | Log-transform and normalize expression data |
| **Data Loading** | `load_data`, `load_multiple_pickles` | Load and combine data from multiple files |
| **Utilities** | `add_zero_padding`, `compute_neighbors` | Zero-padding and neighbor computation |

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:1-175]()

---

## Spatial Upsampling and Smoothing

### Workflow Overview

The spatial upsampling and smoothing pipeline performs clustering-based data augmentation and optional k-nearest neighbor smoothing to improve model training.

```mermaid
graph TB
    INPUT["Input: Gene Counts + Barcodes + Resolution"]
    
    SPLIT["Split by Sample ID"]
    
    subgraph "Per-Sample Processing"
        ADATA["Create AnnData Object"]
        
        CLUSTER_CHOICE{"Clustering Method?"}
        
        DEFAULT["run_default()<br/>PCA + Leiden"]
        AESTETIK["run_aestetik()<br/>AESTETIK + Leiden"]
        
        BALANCE["get_balanced_index()<br/>Balanced Sampling"]
        
        SMOOTH_CHECK{"smooth_n > 0?"}
        
        SMOOTH["KNN Smoothing<br/>NearestNeighbors"]
        
        RESULT["Resampled Barcodes<br/>+ Smoothed Counts"]
    end
    
    COMBINE["Combine All Samples"]
    
    OUTPUT["Output: Augmented Dataset"]
    
    INPUT --> SPLIT
    SPLIT --> ADATA
    
    ADATA --> CLUSTER_CHOICE
    CLUSTER_CHOICE -->|"augmentation='default'"| DEFAULT
    CLUSTER_CHOICE -->|"augmentation='aestetik'"| AESTETIK
    
    DEFAULT --> BALANCE
    AESTETIK --> BALANCE
    
    BALANCE --> SMOOTH_CHECK
    
    SMOOTH_CHECK -->|Yes| SMOOTH
    SMOOTH_CHECK -->|No| RESULT
    SMOOTH --> RESULT
    
    RESULT --> COMBINE
    COMBINE --> OUTPUT
```

**Diagram: Spatial Upsampling and Smoothing Pipeline**

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:65-98]()

### Main Function: spatial_upsample_and_smooth

The `spatial_upsample_and_smooth` function is the entry point for spatial data augmentation.

**Function Signature:**
```python
spatial_upsample_and_smooth(counts, obs, barcode, resolution, smooth_n=0, augmentation="default")
```

**Parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `counts` | `np.ndarray` | Gene expression counts matrix (n_spots × n_genes) |
| `obs` | `pd.DataFrame` | Observation metadata |
| `barcode` | `np.ndarray` | Spot barcodes (must include sample ID) |
| `resolution` | `float` or `None` | Leiden clustering resolution; if `None`, no clustering |
| `smooth_n` | `int` | Number of neighbors for KNN smoothing (default: 0, no smoothing) |
| `augmentation` | `str` | Clustering method: `"default"` or `"aestetik"` |

**Returns:**
- `resampled_barcodes`: NumPy array of balanced barcode samples
- `transcriptomics_smooth`: Smoothed expression counts (zeros if `smooth_n=0`)

**Processing Steps:**

1. **Sample Splitting** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:66-73](): Extracts sample IDs from barcodes (assumes format `*_sampleID_*`) and processes each sample independently

2. **Clustering** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:75-82](): Runs clustering algorithm if `resolution` is specified:
   - `augmentation="default"`: PCA + Leiden clustering
   - `augmentation="aestetik"`: AESTETIK + Leiden clustering

3. **Balanced Sampling** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:86-87](): Uses `get_balanced_index` to oversample minority clusters

4. **KNN Smoothing** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:91-96](): If `smooth_n > 0`, smooths expression by averaging k-nearest neighbors in latent space

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:65-98]()

---

## Clustering Methods

### Default Clustering: run_default

The default clustering method uses standard scanpy preprocessing with PCA dimensionality reduction and Leiden community detection.

```mermaid
graph LR
    INPUT["AnnData Object"]
    
    PCA["sc.pp.pca()<br/>n_comps = min(n_genes-1, 50)"]
    
    NEIGHBORS["sc.pp.neighbors()<br/>Build KNN Graph"]
    
    LEIDEN["sc.tl.leiden()<br/>resolution, flavor='igraph'"]
    
    OUTPUT["Output: adata with<br/>.obsm['latent'] = PCA<br/>.obs['label'] = clusters"]
    
    INPUT --> PCA --> NEIGHBORS --> LEIDEN --> OUTPUT
```

**Diagram: Default Clustering Pipeline**

**Function Signature:**
```python
run_default(adata, resolution=1.0)
```

**Implementation Details:**
- PCA components limited to `min(n_genes - 1, 50)` [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:31]()
- Uses igraph implementation with 2 iterations [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:34]()
- Stores PCA embeddings in `adata.obsm["latent"]`
- Stores cluster labels in `adata.obs["label"]`

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:29-37]()

### AESTETIK Clustering: run_aestetik

AESTETIK (Aesthetic Spatial Transcriptomics) is a multi-modal clustering method that can incorporate both transcriptomic and morphological features. In this implementation, morphology is set to dummy values (weight=0) to focus on transcriptomics.

```mermaid
graph TB
    INPUT["AnnData Object"]
    
    PCA["sc.pp.pca()<br/>Compute PCA"]
    
    SETUP_T["Set Transcriptomics Modality<br/>obsm['X_pca_transcriptomics']"]
    
    SETUP_M["Set Morphology Modality<br/>obsm['X_pca_morphology'] = dummy<br/>(morphology_weight=0)"]
    
    AESTETIK["AESTETIK Model<br/>clustering_method='leiden'<br/>window_size=3"]
    
    FIT["model.fit()"]
    
    PREDICT["model.predict()<br/>cluster=True"]
    
    OUTPUT["Output: adata with<br/>.obsm['latent'] = AESTETIK<br/>.obs['label'] = clusters"]
    
    INPUT --> PCA
    PCA --> SETUP_T
    PCA --> SETUP_M
    SETUP_T --> AESTETIK
    SETUP_M --> AESTETIK
    AESTETIK --> FIT --> PREDICT --> OUTPUT
```

**Diagram: AESTETIK Clustering Pipeline**

**Function Signature:**
```python
run_aestetik(adata, window_size=3, resolution=1.0)
```

**Implementation Details:**
- Requires the `aestetik` package to be installed [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:41]()
- Morphology weight set to 0, focusing only on transcriptomics [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:56]()
- Stores AESTETIK embeddings in `adata.obsm["latent"]`
- Stores cluster labels in `adata.obs["label"]`
- The `nCluster` parameter is set to the `resolution` value for Leiden clustering [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:54]()

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:40-62]()

---

## Balanced Sampling

### get_balanced_index

This function performs balanced resampling to ensure equal representation of all cluster labels.

**Function Signature:**
```python
get_balanced_index(barcode, labels, n_count)
```

**Parameters:**
- `barcode`: Array of spot barcodes
- `labels`: Array of cluster labels (same length as `barcode`)
- `n_count`: Number of samples to draw from each cluster

**Returns:**
- List of resampled barcodes with balanced cluster representation

**Implementation Logic:**

```mermaid
graph LR
    INPUT["barcodes + labels"]
    
    UNIQUE["Get Unique Labels"]
    
    SAMPLE["For each label:<br/>Random sample n_count-1<br/>from that cluster"]
    
    COMBINE["Combine All Samples"]
    
    OUTPUT["Resampled Barcodes"]
    
    INPUT --> UNIQUE --> SAMPLE --> COMBINE --> OUTPUT
```

**Diagram: Balanced Sampling Process**

The function iterates through each unique label and randomly samples `n_count - 1` barcodes from spots with that label [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:24-25](). This ensures that minority clusters are oversampled to match the size of the majority cluster.

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:20-26]()

---

## Normalization and Preprocessing

### log1p_normalization

Performs library size normalization followed by log1p transformation, a standard preprocessing step in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics.

**Function Signature:**
```python
log1p_normalization(arr, factor=10000, eps=1e-12)
```

**Parameters:**
- `arr`: Expression count matrix (n_spots × n_genes)
- `factor`: Normalization factor (default: 10,000 counts per spot)
- `eps`: Small epsilon to prevent division by zero (default: 1e-12)

**Returns:**
- Normalized and log-transformed expression matrix

**Formula:**
```
normalized[i, j] = log(1 + (arr[i, j] / sum(arr[i, :]) + eps) × factor)
```

**Implementation:**
```python
np.log1p(((arr.T / (np.sum(arr, axis=1) + eps)).T) * factor)
```

The function transposes twice to enable proper broadcasting for per-spot normalization [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:129]().

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:128-129]()

### add_zero_padding

Pads an array with zeros to reach a desired size.

**Function Signature:**
```python
add_zero_padding(original_array, desired_padding)
```

**Parameters:**
- `original_array`: NumPy array of shape (n, m)
- `desired_padding`: Target number of rows

**Returns:**
- Padded array of shape (desired_padding, m)

If `original_array.shape[0] == desired_padding`, returns the original array unchanged [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:102-103](). Otherwise, pads with zeros at the bottom [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:107]().

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:101-109]()

```python
load_multiple_pickles(files)
```

**Returns:**

**Implementation:**
```python
pd.concat([pd.read_pickle(f) for f in files])
```

This is a simple wrapper around pandas concatenation [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:125]().

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:124-125]()

### load_data

Comprehensive data loading function that loads gene expression and optionally image features from pickle files.

```mermaid
graph TB
    INPUT["samples list<br/>out_folder path<br/>parameters"]
    
    LOAD_EXPR["Load Gene Expression<br/>from inputX/*.pkl files<br/>load_multiple_pickles()"]
    
    EXTRACT_BC["Extract Barcodes<br/>from DataFrame index"]
    
    CHECK_IMG{"load_image_features?"}
    
    LOAD_IMG["Load Image Features<br/>from image_features/ *.pkl"]
    
    ALIGN["Align to Barcodes<br/>.loc[barcode_list]"]
    
    CHECK_NORM{"raw_counts?"}
    
    NORMALIZE["log1p_normalization()<br/>factor=10000"]
    
    BUILD_DICT["Build Output Dictionary<br/>{'y': expr, 'X': img, 'barcode': bc}"]
    
    OUTPUT["Return data dict"]
    
    INPUT --> LOAD_EXPR
    LOAD_EXPR --> EXTRACT_BC
    EXTRACT_BC --> CHECK_IMG
    
    CHECK_IMG -->|True| LOAD_IMG
    LOAD_IMG --> ALIGN
    
    CHECK_IMG -->|False| CHECK_NORM
    ALIGN --> CHECK_NORM
    
    CHECK_NORM -->|False| NORMALIZE
    CHECK_NORM -->|True| BUILD_DICT
    NORMALIZE --> BUILD_DICT
    
    BUILD_DICT --> OUTPUT
```

**Diagram: load_data Function Flow**

**Function Signature:**
```python
load_data(samples, out_folder, feature_model=None, cell_diameter=None, 
          load_image_features=True, factor=10000, raw_counts=False)
```

**Parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `samples` | `list` | List of sample IDs to load |
| `out_folder` | `str` | Root directory containing data subfolders |
| `feature_model` | `str` | Name of the feature extraction model (e.g., "UNI", "phikon") |
| `cell_diameter` | `int/None` | Cell diameter for diameter-specific features |
| `load_image_features` | `bool` | Whether to load image features (default: True) |
| `factor` | `int` | Normalization factor for log1p (default: 10,000) |
| `raw_counts` | `bool` | If True, skip normalization (default: False) |

**Expected Directory Structure:**
```
out_folder/
├── data/
│   ├── inputX/
│   │   └── {sample}.pkl          # Gene expression data
│   └── image_features/
│       ├── {feature_model}/
│       │   └── {sample}.pkl       # Image features (no diameter)
│       └── {feature_model}_{cell_diameter}/
│           └── {sample}.pkl       # Image features (with diameter)
```

**Returns:**

Dictionary with keys:
- `"y"`: Gene expression matrix (normalized unless `raw_counts=True`)
- `"X"`: Image feature embeddings (if `load_image_features=True`)
- `"barcode"`: Array of spot barcodes

**Processing Details:**

1. **Expression Loading** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:144-149](): Loads expression data from `inputX/{sample}.pkl` files and extracts barcodes from the DataFrame index

2. **Image Feature Loading** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:151-161](): Conditionally loads image features based on whether `cell_diameter` is specified:
   - With diameter: `image_features/{feature_model}_{cell_diameter}/{sample}.pkl`
   - Without diameter: `image_features/{feature_model}/{sample}.pkl`

3. **Alignment** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:155](), [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:160](): Ensures image features align with expression barcodes using `.loc[barcode_list]`

4. **Normalization** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:165-166](): Applies log1p normalization unless `raw_counts=True`

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:132-174]()

---

## Spatial Neighbor Computation

### compute_neighbors

Computes neighboring spots within a specified radius for a given spot based on spatial coordinates.

**Function Signature:**
```python
compute_neighbors(row, coordinates, radius=1)
```

**Parameters:**
- `row`: pandas Series with fields `x_array`, `y_array`, `sampleID`, `barcode`
- `coordinates`: pandas DataFrame containing all spot coordinates with same fields
- `radius`: Integer radius in array units (default: 1)

**Returns:**
- String of neighbor barcodes joined by `"___"`

**Query Logic:**

The function builds a pandas query to find neighbors [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:113-117]():
```python
((x_array - radius) <= row.x_array <= (x_array + radius)) and 
((y_array - radius) <= row.y_array <= (y_array + radius)) and 
(sampleID == row.sampleID and barcode != row.barcode)
```

This finds all spots within a square window of size `(2×radius + 1)` centered on the target spot, excluding the target spot itself and limiting to the same sample.

**Output Format:**

Neighbor barcodes are joined with `"___"` delimiter [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:120](), e.g., `"spot1___spot2___spot3"`.

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:112-121]()

---

| `spatial_upsample_and_smooth` | Data augmentation and smoothing | `resolution`, `smooth_n`, `augmentation` | Resampled barcodes, smoothed counts |
| `run_default` | Default clustering (PCA + Leiden) | `resolution` | AnnData with clusters and latent embeddings |
| `run_aestetik` | AESTETIK clustering | `window_size`, `resolution` | AnnData with AESTETIK embeddings |
| `get_balanced_index` | Balanced cluster sampling | `n_count` | Resampled barcodes |
| `log1p_normalization` | Expression normalization | `factor` (10,000) | Normalized log-transformed array |

| `load_data` | Load expression and features | `samples`, `out_folder`, `feature_model` | Dictionary with expression, features, barcodes |
| `compute_neighbors` | Find spatial neighbors | `radius` | Neighbor barcode string |

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils_dataloader.py:1-175]()

# Page: General Utilities

# General Utilities

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [deepspot2cell/utils/__init__.py](deepspot2cell/utils/__init__.py)
- [deepspot2cell/utils/utils.py](deepspot2cell/utils/utils.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This document covers general-purpose utility functions that support the DeepSpot2Cell pipeline but are not specific to image processing or data loading. These utilities handle configuration management, reproducibility, gene selection, model fine-tuning, inference execution, and result visualization.

For image-specific utilities (PFM loading, tile extraction, spatial prediction), see [Image Processing Utilities](#7.1). For data loading helpers (augmentation, smoothing, clustering), see [Data Loading Utilities](#7.2).

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils.py:1-200](), [deepspot2cell/utils/__init__.py:1-3]()

---

## Utility Function Overview

The general utilities module provides six main categories of functionality that support the DeepSpot2Cell workflow:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Configuration Management"
        load_config["load_config()<br/>YAML → dict"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Reproducibility"
        fix_seed["fix_seed()<br/>Set all random seeds"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Gene Selection"
        order_genes["order_genes()<br/>Variability-based ordering"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Adaptation"
        model_fine_tune["model_fine_tune()<br/>Layer-specific training"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Inference Execution"
        run_inference["run_inference_from_dataloader()<br/>Batch prediction"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Visualization"
        plot_loss["plot_loss_values()<br/>Training curves"]
    end
    
    CONFIG_FILE["config.yaml"] --> load_config
    load_config --> TRAINING["Training Script"]
    
    SEED["Random Seed"] --> fix_seed
    fix_seed --> TRAINING
    
    HEST_DATA["HEST Dataset"] --> order_genes
    order_genes --> GENE_LIST["ordered_genes.json"]
    GENE_LIST --> TRAINING
    
    TRAINED_MODEL["Trained Model"] --> model_fine_tune
    FINETUNE_DATA["Fine-tuning Data"] --> model_fine_tune
    model_fine_tune --> ADAPTED_MODEL["Adapted Model"]
    
    TRAINED_MODEL --> run_inference
    TEST_DATA["Test DataLoader"] --> run_inference
    run_inference --> PREDICTIONS["Predictions Array"]
    
    TRAIN_LOSS["Training Losses"] --> plot_loss
    VAL_LOSS["Validation Losses"] --> plot_loss
    plot_loss --> PLOT["Loss Curve Plot"]
```

**Sources:** [deepspot2cell/utils/utils.py:1-200]()
